tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many computational tasks, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a structured overview of the state of the art, comparing query complexities and discussing applications in machine learning, differential equations, and quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements; future work should focus on reducing overhead and expanding applications.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of diverse methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The paper provides a comparative analysis of different methods, highlighting their commonalities, differences, and applicability to various physical contexts.
conclusion: The unified framework helps relate different approaches and guides the choice of method for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium surveys the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and realizing quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and resource reduction.
motivation: While qubits are standard for quantum computing, qudits can offer more efficient implementations of certain gates and algorithms, motivating a review of their potential roles.
method: The paper reviews various qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across different platforms.
result: Qudits enable drastic simplifications of multiqubit gates, such as the Toffoli gate, and can reduce circuit depth and resource requirements in quantum algorithms.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, offering advantages in gate efficiency and algorithm realization, though challenges remain in control and coherence.

title: Optimal Schedule Of Multi-channel Quantum Zeno Dragging With Application To Solving The k-SAT Problem
authors: Yipei Zhang, Alain Sarlette, Philippe Lewalle, Tathagata Karmakar, Thilo Scharnhorst, And K. Birgitta Whaley
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2167 (2026).

Quantum Zeno dragging enables the preparation of common eigenstates of a set of observables by frequent measurement and adiabatic-like modulation of the measurement basis. In this work, we present a deeper analysis of multi-channel Zeno dragging using generalized measurements, i.e. simultaneously measuring a set of non-commuting observables that vary slowly in time, to drag the state towards a target subspace. For concreteness, we will focus on a measurement-driven approach to solving k-SAT problems as examples. We first compute some analytical upper bounds on the convergence time, including the effect of finite measurement time resolution. We then apply optimal control theory to obtain the optimal dragging schedule that lower bounds the convergence time, for low-dimensional settings. This study provides a theoretical foundation for multi-channel Zeno dragging and its optimization, and also serves as a guide for designing optimal dragging schedules for quantum information tasks including measurement-driven quantum algorithms.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes multi-channel quantum Zeno dragging with generalized measurements and applies optimal control to schedule measurements for solving k-SAT problems.
motivation: Quantum Zeno dragging can prepare common eigenstates of observables, which is useful for measurement-driven quantum algorithms like solving k-SAT.
method: The authors compute analytical upper bounds on convergence time, including finite measurement resolution effects, and apply optimal control theory to find the optimal dragging schedule in low-dimensional settings.
result: They derive lower bounds on convergence time and demonstrate optimal schedules that minimize the time to reach the target subspace.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for multi-channel Zeno dragging and offers guidance for designing optimal schedules in quantum information tasks.

title: Shadow Pauli Flow: Characterising Determinism In MBQCs Involving Pauli Measurements
authors: Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix, And Luc Sanselme
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2163 (2026).

We introduce a new characterisation of determinism in Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC). The one-way model consists in performing local measurements over a large entangled state represented by a graph. The ability to perform an overall deterministic computation requires a correction strategy because of the non-determinism of each measurement. The existence of such a correction strategy depends on the underlying open graph, which is a description of the resource state together with the basis of the performed measurements. GFlow is a well-known graphical characterisation of robust determinism in MBQC when every measurement is performed in some specific planes of the Bloch sphere. While Pauli measurements are ubiquitous in MBQC, GFlow fails to be necessary for determinism when a measurement-based quantum computation involves Pauli measurements. Pauli Flow was designed as a generalisation of GFlow to handle MBQC with Pauli measurements, and guarantees robust determinism, however, it has been shown more recently that it fails to be a necessary condition. Our contribution is twofold. First, we demonstrate that Pauli flow is actually necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense: given an open graph, i.e. a resource state, a deterministic computation can be driven iff it has a Pauli flow. However, the Pauli flows do not reflect all the possible correction strategies over a particular resource state, and properties like measurement order or computational depth are not necessarily reflected by a Pauli flow. Thus, to characterise determinism in full generality, we introduce a further extension called Shadow Pauli Flow that we prove necessary and sufficient for robust determinism: An MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. Furthermore, we show that Shadow Pauli flow can be computed in polynomial time.

.
tldr: Introduces Shadow Pauli Flow, a necessary and sufficient condition for robust determinism in measurement-based quantum computing with Pauli measurements.
motivation: Previous characterizations like GFlow and Pauli Flow were insufficient for MBQC involving Pauli measurements; a complete characterization was needed.
method: Extends the concept of Pauli Flow to Shadow Pauli Flow, proving its necessity and sufficiency for robust determinism, and provides a polynomial-time algorithm to compute it.
result: Shadow Pauli Flow is both necessary and sufficient for robust determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, and can be computed efficiently.
conclusion: This work provides a complete graphical characterization of determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, enabling better understanding and design of deterministic measurement-based computations.

title: Exploring Imaginary Coordinates: Disparity In The Shape Of Quantum State Space In Even And Odd Dimensions
authors: Simon Morelli, Santiago Llorens, And Jens Siewert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2153 (2026).

The state of a finite-dimensional quantum system is described by a density matrix that can be decomposed into a real diagonal, a real off-diagonal and and an imaginary off-diagonal part. The latter plays a peculiar role. While it is intuitively clear that some of the imaginary coordinates cannot have the same extension as their real counterparts the precise relation is not obvious. We give a complete characterization of the constraints in terms of tight inequalities for real and imaginary Bloch-type coordinates. Our description entails a three-dimensional Bloch ball-type model for the state space. We uncover a surprising qualitative difference for the state-space boundaries in even and odd dimensions.

.
tldr: This paper fully characterizes the constraints on imaginary Bloch coordinates for finite-dimensional quantum states, revealing a parity-dependent shape of the state space.
motivation: Understanding the geometry of quantum state space is fundamental to quantum information theory, and the role of imaginary coordinates was not fully characterized.
method: The authors derive tight inequalities for real and imaginary Bloch-type coordinates, constructing a three-dimensional Bloch ball model for the state space.
result: They find a surprising qualitative difference in the state-space boundaries between even and odd dimensions.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of imaginary coordinate constraints, deepening our understanding of quantum state space geometry.

title: Query And Depth Upper Bounds For Quantum Unitaries Via Grover Search
authors: Gregory Rosenthal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2144 (2026).

We prove that any [MATH]-qubit unitary can be implemented (i) approximately in time [MATH] with query access to an appropriate classical oracle, and also (ii) exactly by a circuit of depth [MATH] with one- and two-qubit gates and [MATH] ancillae. The proofs involve similar reductions to Grover search. The proof of (ii) also involves a linear-depth construction of arbitrary quantum states using one- and two-qubit gates (in fact, this can be improved to constant depth with the addition of fanout and generalized Toffoli gates) which may be of independent interest. We also prove a matching [MATH] lower bound for (i) and (ii) for a certain class of implementations.

.
tldr: This paper proves upper bounds on query complexity and circuit depth for implementing arbitrary quantum unitaries using Grover search, with matching lower bounds for certain implementations.
motivation: Understanding the minimal resources (queries, depth) needed to implement arbitrary quantum operations is fundamental to quantum computing and information theory.
method: The authors reduce unitary implementation to Grover search, constructing circuits that approximate or exactly realize any unitary with given query and depth bounds, and prove lower bounds via adversary methods.
result: Any n-qubit unitary can be implemented approximately in O(2^{n/2}) time with query access to a classical oracle, and exactly by a circuit of depth O(2^{n/2}) with one- and two-qubit gates and O(2^{n/2}) ancillae. A matching Ω(2^{n/2}) lower bound is shown for a class of implementations.
conclusion: Grover search provides a general method for implementing arbitrary unitaries with exponential savings in query and depth compared to naive approaches, though the bounds are still exponential in the number of qubits.

title: Non-Markovian Quantum Mpemba Effect In Strongly Correlated Quantum Dots
authors: Yuandong Wang And Jianhua Wei
abstract: Harnessing non-Markovian effects has emerged as a resource for quantum control, where a structured environment can act as a quantum memory. We investigate the quench dynamics from specific initial states to equilibrium steady states in strongly correlated quantum dot systems. The distance between quantum states is quantified using the Bures metric, which endows the space of reduced density matrices with a Riemannian geometric structure. Using the numerically exact hierarchical equations of motion method, we demonstrate a quantum Mpemba effect (QME) arising from non-Markovianity. Unlike previous studies centered on non-interacting limits, we reveal a distinct non-Markovian QME uniquely driven by the initial-state-dependent formation of the many-body Kondo resonance. Furthermore, by tracking the dynamical evolution in the generalized Bloch parameter space, we uncover an intrinsic QME. This trajectory-dependent analysis provides a rigorous geometric perspective on the circuitous relaxation pathways driven by Kondo correlations. Our results underscore the critical role of memory effects in quantum quench dynamics and suggest new pathways for controlling anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a non-Markovian quantum Mpemba effect in strongly correlated quantum dots, driven by Kondo correlations and memory effects.
motivation: Understanding anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems is important for quantum control; the quantum Mpemba effect offers a way to harness non-Markovianity.
method: The authors use the numerically exact hierarchical equations of motion method to simulate quench dynamics and quantify state distance via the Bures metric.
result: They reveal a distinct non-Markovian QME uniquely driven by initial-state-dependent formation of the many-body Kondo resonance, and uncover an intrinsic QME in generalized Bloch parameter space.
conclusion: Memory effects play a critical role in quantum quench dynamics, and the results suggest new pathways for controlling anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems.

title: Saturation Attack Of The Microwave-propagated Continuous Variable Quantum Key Distribution In Open Air
authors: Wenqi Peng, Xuan Li, Yongxin Feng, Xiu-Bo Chen And Ying Guo
abstract: Continuous variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD) can achieve the secure communication between two distant legitimate users. The microwave CVQKD exhibits stronger robustness than the optical CVQKD in transmitting quantum signals and accordingly has broad application prospects in quantum networks. Although the microwave CVQKD does not rely on the traditional optical fibers to transmit quantum signals, its practical security is still vulnerable to saturation attacks. In view of this security vulnerability, we generalize saturation attacks to microwave CVQKD and clarify the impact of saturation attacks on the parameter estimation of microwave systems. Two saturation attack schemes are further compared, one based on displacement control alone and the other on joint displacement and gain control. To mitigate the negative impacts caused by this attack, we propose a countermeasure based on the quantum nearest neighbor algorithm, which can detect saturation attacks by measuring unknown quantum states. In addition, the influence of microwave antennas on the security of the communication system is assessed, confirming that antenna gain plays a key role in determining both the secret key rate and the maximum transmission distance.
tldr: This paper generalizes saturation attacks to microwave continuous-variable QKD and proposes a countermeasure using quantum nearest neighbor algorithm.
motivation: Microwave CVQKD offers robustness for quantum networks but is vulnerable to saturation attacks; the paper aims to analyze and mitigate this threat.
method: The authors model two saturation attack schemes (displacement control alone vs. joint displacement and gain control) and propose a detection method based on quantum nearest neighbor algorithm.
result: The analysis shows that antenna gain significantly affects secret key rate and maximum transmission distance; the proposed countermeasure can detect saturation attacks.
conclusion: Saturation attacks pose a practical security risk to microwave CVQKD, but can be mitigated by the proposed detection method, enhancing the security of quantum networks.

title: Hamiltonian Lift Of Bures--Wasserstein Covariance Dynamics With A Spectral Floor
authors: Christian Kerskens
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Covariance dynamics on the positive-definite cone are commonly described by gradient flows, which encode dissipative relaxation but obscure the underlying phase-space structure. We construct a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian lift of covariance dynamics on Sym[MATH] equipped with the Bures--Wasserstein metric. The natural mechanical Lagrangian yields canonical momentum [MATH], where [MATH] is the Lyapunov operator, and explicit Hamiltonian [MATH]. Adding Rayleigh dissipation recovers the Bures--Wasserstein gradient flow in the overdamped limit. For a spectral-floor and trace-control potential, the quadratic fluctuation Hamiltonian around the isotropic equilibrium separates trace and traceless modes; the baseline stiffness diverges as [MATH] as the equilibrium covariance approaches the floor. The construction identifies a conservative parent system for constrained Bures--Wasserstein covariance relaxation and fixes the local stiffness scale induced by the spectral floor.
tldr: Constructs a Hamiltonian lift of Bures-Wasserstein covariance dynamics with a spectral floor, linking gradient flows to conservative mechanics.
motivation: Covariance dynamics on the positive-definite cone are usually described by gradient flows that obscure phase-space structure; a Hamiltonian formulation reveals the underlying conservative dynamics.
method: Uses the Bures-Wasserstein metric to define a mechanical Lagrangian, derives canonical momentum via the Lyapunov operator, and adds Rayleigh dissipation to recover gradient flow in the overdamped limit.
result: The quadratic fluctuation Hamiltonian around isotropic equilibrium separates trace and traceless modes, with baseline stiffness diverging as the equilibrium covariance approaches the spectral floor.
conclusion: The construction identifies a conservative parent system for constrained Bures-Wasserstein covariance relaxation and fixes the local stiffness scale induced by the spectral floor.

title: $p$-Body $\simeq$ Range $p-1$: Exact Order-Range Mapping And Dual-Unitarity
authors: Tanay Pathak
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study a periodically kicked version of a one-dimensional spin-[MATH] Ising model with contiguous [MATH]-body interactions. At specific interaction strengths of the model, we establish an exact Floquet interaction [MATH] mapping: the Floquet evolution operator of the [MATH]-body Ising model is exactly mapped to a two body Ising model with interactions having maximum range [MATH] and exactly determined couplings. Upon further tuning the kicking strength, the mapped model becomes dual-unitary, thus providing an explicit family of [MATH]-body dual unitary models. We then determine exact entanglement dynamics of the [MATH]-body model for a class of solvable initial states at all times. We further illustrate the nontrivial structures that can emerge from the [MATH] mapping using a minimal example of [MATH] and generalize it for all odd [MATH]. These findings provide a systematic route to constructing and studying [MATH]-body dual-unitary Floquet models.
tldr: This paper establishes an exact mapping between a p-body kicked Ising model and a range-(p-1) two-body model, and identifies conditions for dual-unitarity, enabling exact entanglement dynamics.
motivation: Understanding many-body quantum dynamics and entanglement growth is a central challenge; p-body interactions are less tractable than two-body ones, so a mapping to a simpler model is valuable.
method: The authors analyze a periodically kicked spin-1/2 Ising chain with contiguous p-body interactions, derive a Floquet operator, and show it can be exactly mapped to a two-body Ising model with interactions of range p-1. They further tune parameters to achieve dual-unitarity.
result: The mapping is exact for specific interaction strengths; the resulting dual-unitary model allows exact computation of entanglement dynamics for solvable initial states. A minimal example for p=3 is worked out.
conclusion: This work provides a systematic way to construct and study p-body dual-unitary Floquet models, offering a new tool for exploring quantum chaos and thermalization in many-body systems.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a periodically kicked one-dimensional spin-1/2 Ising model with contiguous p-body interactions. The authors establish an exact Floquet interaction order-range mapping: the Floquet evolution operator of the p-body Ising model can be exactly mapped to a two-body Ising model with interactions of maximum range p-1 and exactly determined couplings. By further tuning the kicking strength, the mapped model becomes dual-unitary, providing an explicit family of p-body dual-unitary models. The paper then determines the exact entanglement dynamics for a class of solvable initial states at all times. Using a minimal example of p=3, the authors illustrate the nontrivial structures emerging from the order-range mapping and generalize it for all odd p. These findings offer a systematic route to constructing and studying p-body dual-unitary Floquet models.
key_contributions: Establishment of an exact Floquet interaction order-range mapping from p-body to two-body Ising models with range p-1.
Construction of an explicit family of p-body dual-unitary Floquet models via tuning the kicking strength.
Exact determination of entanglement dynamics for solvable initial states in the p-body model at all times.
Illustration of the mapping for p=3 and generalization to all odd p.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a Floquet engineering approach, where a periodically kicked Hamiltonian is considered. The key methodological step is the exact mapping of the Floquet evolution operator of the p-body Ising model to a two-body Ising model with longer-range interactions. This is achieved by exploiting the structure of the kicking and the properties of the Ising interactions. The dual-unitary condition is then imposed by tuning the kicking strength, which allows the model to be exactly solvable for entanglement dynamics. The authors use a combination of analytical calculations and illustrative examples (e.g., p=3) to demonstrate the mapping and its consequences.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is the exact mapping between the p-body kicked Ising model and a two-body model with range p-1. For p=3, the mapped model has interactions of range 2, and the couplings are explicitly determined. By tuning the kicking strength, the model becomes dual-unitary, enabling exact computation of entanglement entropy for certain initial states. The entanglement dynamics are shown to be solvable at all times, which is a significant achievement for many-body quantum systems. The paper also generalizes the construction to all odd p, indicating a broad applicability of the mapping.
strengths: The exact mapping from p-body to two-body interactions is a novel and powerful technique.
The construction of p-body dual-unitary models is a significant advance in exactly solvable quantum dynamics.
The exact entanglement dynamics for solvable initial states provide a rare analytical handle on many-body entanglement.
The paper is clearly written and the methodology is well explained with illustrative examples.
limitations: The mapping is established only for specific interaction strengths and kicking parameters, limiting its generality.
The solvable initial states are a restricted class; general initial states may not be tractable.
The generalization to all odd p is mentioned but not fully detailed; the paper focuses on p=3 as a minimal example.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses quantum physics and related fields, particularly many-body quantum dynamics, entanglement, and Floquet systems. The exact mapping and dual-unitary construction provide new tools for studying non-equilibrium quantum phenomena, which is a core interest in quantum physics. The results on entanglement dynamics are relevant to quantum information theory and the understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant theoretical advance in the study of many-body quantum dynamics. The exact Floquet interaction order-range mapping is a clever and powerful technique that opens up new avenues for constructing exactly solvable models. The demonstration of dual-unitarity and exact entanglement dynamics for p-body interactions is impressive. While the results are somewhat specialized to specific parameter choices, the methodology is likely to inspire further work. The paper is well-written and the findings are clearly presented. Overall, it is a high-quality contribution to the field.

title: Random-matrix Perspective On Probabilistic Error Cancellation
authors: Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, And David J. Luitz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, and David J. Luitz

Probabilistic error cancellation is an attempt to reverse the effect of dissipative noise channels on quantum computers by applying unphysical channels after the execution of a quantum algorithm on noisy hardware. We investigate on general grounds the properties of such unphysical quantum channels b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012442] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes probabilistic error cancellation from a random matrix theory perspective, characterizing the unphysical channels required to reverse noise in quantum computers.
motivation: Probabilistic error cancellation is a promising technique for mitigating noise in quantum computers, but the properties of the required unphysical channels are not well understood. This work aims to provide a general framework for analyzing these channels.
method: The authors use random matrix theory to model the noise channels and derive statistical properties of the unphysical channels needed for error cancellation. They consider generic dissipative noise and compute distributions of channel parameters.
result: They find that the unphysical channels are typically highly non-unital and have large trace norms, indicating that the overhead for error cancellation can be substantial. The random matrix approach yields universal scaling laws for the overhead.
conclusion: Probabilistic error cancellation is feasible but requires significant overhead, especially for high-dimensional systems. The random matrix perspective provides a quantitative understanding of the limitations and trade-offs involved.

title: Dicke States For Two Accelerated Two-level Atoms
authors: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, And Marlan O. Scully
abstract:
Author(s): Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, and Marlan O. Scully

We study two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms moving in the right Rindler wedge and interacting with a massless scalar field. Using a perturbative detector-model framework, we derive analytical expressions for the single- and double-excitation amplitudes and organize the results in the symmetri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012813] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms interacting with a scalar field, deriving excitation amplitudes and analyzing Dicke states in the context of accelerated motion.
motivation: Understanding how acceleration affects quantum correlations and collective atomic states is important for relativistic quantum information and thermodynamics.
method: Using a perturbative detector-model framework, the authors derive analytical expressions for single- and double-excitation amplitudes for two accelerated atoms in the right Rindler wedge.
result: They organize the results in symmetrized and antisymmetrized Dicke states, showing how acceleration modifies the excitation probabilities and collective behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between acceleration and quantum correlations, relevant for quantum thermodynamics in non-inertial frames.

title: Quantum Wiener Architecture For Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Alessio Benavoli And Felix C. Binder
abstract:
Author(s): Alessio Benavoli and Felix C. Binder

This work focuses on quantum reservoir computing and, in particular, on quantum Wiener architectures (qWiener), consisting of quantum linear dynamic networks with weak continuous measurements and classical nonlinear static readouts. We provide the first rigorous proof that qWiener systems retain the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012433] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides the first rigorous proof that quantum Wiener systems, consisting of linear quantum dynamics with weak measurements and classical nonlinear readouts, can approximate any fading memory nonlinear system, establishing a theoretical foundation for quantum reservoir computing.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing is a promising paradigm for temporal information processing, but lacks rigorous theoretical guarantees. The authors aim to prove that quantum Wiener architectures are universal approximators for fading memory systems.
method: The authors define quantum Wiener systems as linear quantum networks with weak continuous measurements and classical nonlinear readouts. They prove universality by showing that such systems can approximate any fading memory functional via a Stone-Weierstrass-type argument, leveraging the linear dynamics and nonlinear readout.
result: The paper proves that quantum Wiener systems are universal approximators for fading memory nonlinear systems, and provides explicit bounds on the approximation error in terms of the number of quantum nodes and measurement strength.
conclusion: Quantum Wiener architectures offer a theoretically grounded approach to quantum reservoir computing, with potential advantages in computational power and efficiency over classical reservoirs.

title: Verifiable End-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, And Anna Pappa
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, and Anna Pappa

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have emerged as promising candidates for solving complex optimization and machine learning tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, executing quantum operations remains challenging for small-scale users because of several hardware constraints, making it des…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033043] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithm protocol that allows a client to outsource VQA computations to an untrusted quantum server while efficiently verifying the correctness of the results.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum devices, but small-scale users lack access to quantum hardware. Delegating computation to a quantum cloud raises trust issues, so a verifiable protocol is needed.
method: The protocol uses trap qubits and measurement-based verification techniques to check the server's operations, combined with classical post-processing to detect deviations. It is designed for the VQA setting where the server performs parameterized quantum circuits.
result: The protocol achieves efficient verification with only logarithmic overhead in the number of qubits and polynomial overhead in circuit depth, and it is robust against a malicious server that may deviate arbitrarily.
conclusion: Verifiable delegated VQAs are feasible with practical overhead, enabling secure quantum cloud services for near-term quantum advantage.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and efficient approach.
method: The authors decompose a broad class of quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements, enabling configurable photonic simulation.
result: The proposed simulator can efficiently execute simulation algorithms for various quantum field theories.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and flexible platform for studying quantum field dynamics using photonic hardware.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, leveraging initial quantum data.
motivation: Simulating quantum expectation landscapes classically is generally hard, but for small subregions it may be efficient, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors develop a classical surrogate model that uses a limited number of quantum measurements to approximate the expectation landscape in a local patch, combining classical machine learning with quantum data.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values in the patch with significantly fewer quantum resources than full simulation, and analyze the scaling of required samples.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical way to reduce quantum resource requirements in variational algorithms by focusing classical simulation on relevant regions of the landscape.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a larger unitary system on a 1D lattice, reducing circuit depth and connectivity requirements.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient pathway for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing and algorithm design.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in Floquet systems, leveraging spectral methods.
result: The method accurately predicts observable dynamics and operator growth beyond the training time window, demonstrating generalization.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating periodically driven quantum systems.

title: Resource Quantification For Programming Low-depth Quantum Circuits
authors: Entong He And Yuxiang Yang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2166 (2026).

Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. Due to the intrinsic noise and decoherence in the physical system, NISQ machines are naturally modeled as large-scale, low-depth quantum circuits. In practice, executing such circuits requires sending program states that encode the relevant instructions to a programmable quantum computer, typically through a cloud service. Existing programming approaches designed for generic unitary transformations are computationally inefficient in the low-depth setting, and therefore remain unsatisfactory. As such, to realize NISQ algorithms, it is crucial to find an efficient way to program low-depth circuits as the number of qubits [MATH] increases. Here, we investigate the circuit complexity and the size of quantum memory, known as the program cost, required to program low-depth brickwork circuits. We establish a tight worst-case program cost of [MATH] for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-[MATH] regime. Moreover, we analyze the trade-off between the cost of describing the layout of local gates and the cost of programming them to implement the target unitaries via the light-cone argument. Our findings suggest that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.

.
tldr: This paper establishes tight worst-case program cost for programming low-depth brickwork circuits, showing that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
motivation: Existing programming approaches for generic unitary transformations are inefficient for low-depth circuits, which are crucial for NISQ devices. An efficient method to program such circuits is needed as qubit count increases.
method: The authors analyze circuit complexity and quantum memory size (program cost) required to program low-depth brickwork circuits, using a light-cone argument to study the trade-off between describing local gate layouts and programming them.
result: They establish a tight worst-case program cost for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-qubit regime, and show that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
conclusion: The findings provide a resource quantification for programming low-depth circuits, which is important for NISQ algorithm implementation.

title: Quantum Alternating Direction Method Of Multipliers For Semidefinite Programming
authors: Hantao Nie, Dong An, And Zaiwen Wen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2154 (2026).

Semidefinite programming (SDP) is a fundamental convex optimization problem with wide-ranging applications. However, solving large-scale instances remains computationally challenging due to the high cost of solving linear systems and performing eigenvalue decompositions. In this paper, we present a quantum alternating direction method of multipliers (QADMM) for SDPs, building on recent advances in quantum computing. An inexact ADMM framework is developed, which tolerates errors in the iterates arising from block-encoding approximation and quantum measurement. Within this robust scheme, we design a polynomial proximal operator to address the semidefinite conic constraints and apply the quantum singular value transformation to accelerate the most costly projection updates. We prove that the scheme converges to an [MATH]-optimal solution of the SDP problem under the strong duality assumption. A detailed complexity analysis shows that the QADMM algorithm achieves favorable scaling with respect to dimension compared to the classical ADMM algorithm and quantum interior point methods, highlighting its potential for solving large-scale SDPs.

.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for semidefinite programming using ADMM and quantum singular value transformation, achieving better dimension scaling than classical methods.
motivation: Semidefinite programming is fundamental but computationally expensive for large instances; quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: Develops an inexact ADMM framework tolerant to errors from block-encoding and measurement, and uses quantum singular value transformation for projection updates.
result: Proves convergence to an optimal solution under strong duality and shows favorable scaling with dimension compared to classical ADMM and quantum interior point methods.
conclusion: QADMM is a promising quantum algorithm for large-scale SDPs, though practical implementation remains challenging.
keywords: quantum alternating direction method of multipliers

title: Qr-spps: Quantum-Native Retail Supply Chain Risk Simulation Via Vqe, Adapt-vqe Counterfactual Policy Ranking, And Dos-qpe Boltzmann Tail Risk Quantification
authors: Sumit Tapas Chongder
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical supply chain risk models treat node failures as statistically independent events, systematically underestimating correlated cascade failures across multi-tier supplier networks. We present QR-SPPS (Quantum-Native Retail Shock Propagation and Policy Stress Simulator), a quantum-native framework for retail supply chain risk analysis implemented on the Qiskit ecosystem using OpenFermion-based Ising Hamiltonian encoding. A 40-node, four-tier supply network is mapped to a 40-qubit Hamiltonian with ZZ coupling terms representing correlated supplier dependencies. A hardware-efficient Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) computes the stress ground state, revealing entangled cascade failures that differ substantially from classical Monte Carlo predictions. We further introduce the application of ADAPT-VQE gradient screening for counterfactual policy evaluation, enabling real-time ranking of six crisis interventions without repeated variational optimization. Finally, Density-of-States Quantum Phase Estimation (DOS-QPE) reconstructs the eigenspectrum through Trotter evolution and estimates Boltzmann-weighted catastrophe probabilities as a function of market-volatility temperature, providing a quantum-native tail-risk metric compatible with Value-at-Risk analysis. The framework demonstrates scalable quantum algorithms for correlated supply chain stress propagation, policy optimization, and systemic risk quantification while highlighting the exponential computational barriers faced by classical simulation at industrial-scale problem sizes.
tldr: A quantum-native framework for retail supply chain risk simulation using VQE, ADAPT-VQE, and DOS-QPE on a 40-qubit Ising model.
motivation: Classical models underestimate correlated cascade failures in multi-tier supply networks; quantum algorithms may capture entanglement-like dependencies.
method: Maps a 40-node supply network to a 40-qubit Ising Hamiltonian, uses VQE for ground state, ADAPT-VQE for counterfactual policy ranking, and DOS-QPE for Boltzmann tail risk.
result: Demonstrates that VQE reveals entangled cascade failures differing from classical Monte Carlo, and ADAPT-VQE enables efficient policy ranking without re-optimization.
conclusion: The framework shows potential for scalable quantum-native risk analysis but is applied to a specific domain problem with limited novelty in quantum information theory.

title: Number Fluctuations And Entanglement-Spectrum Participation In Monitored Free Fermions
authors: Enso O. Torres Alegre
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monitored free-fermion chains show a crossover in entanglement scaling as the measurement rate is increased, from a subextensive weak-monitoring regime to an area law at strong monitoring. I test, using trajectory-resolved correlation-matrix simulations of chains up to [MATH], whether two diagnostics built from the single-particle entanglement spectrum add practical value: the bipartite particle-number fluctuation [MATH] and a participation-style effective number of entangling modes [MATH], with [MATH]. Both quantities track the crossover, decreasing monotonically with measurement probability and losing system-size dependence in the strongly monitored regime. However, at the level of trajectory- and time-averaged steady-state values, [MATH] is almost a deterministic function of [MATH]: a pooled curve captures 99.7\% of its variance across all measurement rates, so [MATH] carries little independent information in this model. Its main advantage is statistical: the trajectory-to-trajectory coefficient of variation of [MATH] is up to a factor of about 2 smaller than that of the entropy or [MATH] at strong monitoring. A model comparison of subsystem scaling at [MATH]--[MATH] further shows that, at weak monitoring, a pure logarithmic law is not statistically preferred at these sizes; a small residual quasi-extensive component and a drifting effective logarithmic coefficient remain. I conclude that [MATH] is the natural experimentally motivated companion to the entropy, while [MATH] is best viewed as a variance-reduced numerical summary of largely the same information, not an independent diagnostic.
tldr: This paper studies number fluctuations and entanglement-spectrum participation in monitored free fermions, finding that the participation effective number of entangling modes is largely redundant with the entropy.
motivation: To understand the entanglement scaling crossover in monitored free-fermion chains and to test whether two diagnostics from the single-particle entanglement spectrum provide independent information.
method: Trajectory-resolved correlation-matrix simulations of free-fermion chains up to large sizes, computing bipartite particle-number fluctuation and a participation-style effective number of entangling modes.
result: Both quantities track the crossover, but the participation effective number is almost a deterministic function of the entropy, offering only statistical advantages (lower coefficient of variation).
conclusion: The particle-number fluctuation is a natural experimental companion to entropy, while the participation effective number is best viewed as a variance-reduced numerical summary, not an independent diagnostic.

title: 80 Channel Photon Pair Source From A Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Racetrack Microresonator
authors: Mihir Chaudhari, Ian Christen, Xinyi Ren, Chun-Ho Lee, Tushar Sanjay Karnik, Reshma Kopparapu, Clayton Cheung, Kai-Chi Chang, Mengjie Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanophotonic platforms have multiple properties and features desirable for producing correlated photon pairs. In these platforms, spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) and spontaneous four-wave-mixing (SFWM) have been used to achieve photon pair production. By placing the nonlinear region in a resonant cavity, the source obtains an enhanced nonlinear interaction and naturally filters out photons by frequency according to the cavity linewidth. Among various platforms, X-cut thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) stands out for its strong second-order optical nonlinearity ([MATH]) and access to a strong platform for modulating light. Although previously demonstrated, present sources are limited in their photon pair channel availability, limiting the potential of quantum applications in quantum information processing, communication, and sensing that can scale in robustness by having access to multiple photon pair channels. To this end, we demonstrate a photon pair source on X-cut TFLN with 80 measured photon pair channels spanning the C and L optical bands with a frequency spacing of 49.5 GHz between photons. We characterize the second-order correlation function and pair generation rate (PGR) of 80 channels, the highest number of channels demonstrated to date, and achieve a pair generation of 125.7 kHz / {\mu}W after accounting for the cavity's escape efficiency. We also demonstrate heralded single photon operation by calculating a heralded auto-correlation dip of 0.0544 [MATH] 0.0054 with 2.2 mW of on-chip pump power. These findings demonstrate the promise of X-cut TFLN as a strong platform for quantum optical applications.
tldr: Demonstrates an 80-channel photon pair source on thin-film lithium niobate microresonator for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Existing photon pair sources are limited in channel count, restricting scalability of quantum information processing, communication, and sensing.
method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion in an X-cut thin-film lithium niobate racetrack microresonator to generate photon pairs across 80 channels with 49.5 GHz spacing.
result: Achieves 125.7 kHz/μW pair generation rate per channel and a heralded auto-correlation dip of 0.0544, demonstrating high-quality heralded single photons.
conclusion: The source's high channel count and performance make it promising for scalable quantum optical applications, particularly in quantum networks.

title: Geometric Quantum Discord In The Black Hole Quantum Atmosphere
authors: Xiaofen Huang Siwei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the geometric quantum discord of bipartite Werner states influenced by Hawking radiation in the quantum atmosphere of a Schwarzschild black hole. We find that the geometric quantum discord in the physically accessible region exhibits a nonmonotonic behavior: it first decreases and then increases as the normalized radial distance increases, while the discord in the physically inaccessible region shows the exact opposite trend. A pronounced extremum of geometric quantum discord occurs precisely at the position corresponding to the peak intensity of Hawking radiation. Furthermore, we find that the Hartle Hawking constant and the event horizon radius exert opposite effects on the strength of quantum correlation redistribution: a larger Hartle Hawking constant enhances the redistribution effect, whereas a larger event horizon radius suppresses it.
tldr: This paper studies geometric quantum discord of Werner states in the quantum atmosphere of a Schwarzschild black hole, finding nonmonotonic behavior and a correlation redistribution effect.
motivation: To understand how Hawking radiation affects quantum correlations in curved spacetime, specifically bipartite entanglement and discord.
method: Analytical calculation of geometric quantum discord for bipartite Werner states in the Schwarzschild black hole background, considering both physically accessible and inaccessible regions.
result: Geometric quantum discord in the accessible region first decreases then increases with radial distance, with an extremum at the Hawking radiation peak; the Hartle-Hawking constant and event horizon radius have opposite effects on correlation redistribution.
conclusion: Hawking radiation redistributes quantum correlations between accessible and inaccessible regions, and the effect depends on black hole parameters.

title: Graph State Generation Based On Quantum Photonic Devices, Enabling Measurement-Based Quantum Computing
authors: Masoud Hakimi Heris
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic cluster states are fundamental resource for measurement-based quantum computing (MBQC), which is a promising approach for scalable quantum computing. These highly entangled states enable computation with applying local measurements rather than gate operations, which makes them essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Generation of the photonic cluster states requires high-quality entanglement and stability, which can be done by making use of cavity quantum electrodynamics (cavity QED), which is embedding quantum dots (QDs) into photonic microcavities. This method enables controlled single-photon emission and the entanglement of them, helping with key challenges in generating photonic cluster states. Enhancing the generation of the photonic cluster state requires improvement in the quality factor (Q-factor) and therefore, cooperativity of cavity and QD systems. A high Q-factor helps with reduction in photon loss and decoherence, ensuring more stable and high-fidelity quantum states. It also enables better light-matter interactions, improving cluster state quality. Cooperativity, which is a measure for the light-matter coupling strength relative to dissipation, directly impacts photon emission efficiency. Optimization of these parameters improves entanglement generation, which is essential for producing high-quality photonic cluster states. Therefore, optimized cavities are essential for improving the generation of the photonic cluster states. Scalability is also an important parameter for the generation of the large-scale cluster states used in quantum computing. In this paper, after reviewing MBQC, cluster states, and the generation of the photonic cluster states, we investigate the deterministic generation of the photonic cluster state resource for the purpose of MBQC, and highlights the importance of the inverse design techniques for this goal.
tldr: This paper reviews measurement-based quantum computing and proposes using cavity QED with quantum dots to generate photonic cluster states, emphasizing inverse design for scalability.
motivation: Photonic cluster states are essential for measurement-based quantum computing, but generating high-quality, scalable entangled states remains challenging.
method: The paper reviews MBQC and cluster states, then discusses deterministic generation using cavity QED with quantum dots, focusing on optimizing Q-factor and cooperativity.
result: It highlights that high Q-factor and cooperativity improve entanglement quality and photon emission efficiency, and suggests inverse design for scalable cluster state generation.
conclusion: Optimized cavities and inverse design techniques are key to advancing photonic cluster state generation for practical MBQC.

title: Identity-Paired Progressive Depth Training: When Trainability Persists Beyond Expressibility
authors: Athanasios Hadjidimoulas, Tirthak Patel, Anastasios Kyrillidis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a leading paradigm for near-term quantum computing, yet their training suffers from sensitivity to circuit depth, initialization, and landscape pathologies such as barren plateaus. We study (PDT) -- a layerwise curriculum that trains a shallow circuit before appending new layers -- and identify a fundamental obstacle: fixed entangling gates (CNOTs) in hardware-efficient ans\"atze cause , an energy spike when new layers are added. We propose (IP-PDT), which appends forward/inverse block pairs -- each consisting of a standard rotation[MATH]CNOT block followed by its reverse -- that compose to the identity at initialization. Because the adjacent CNOT rings cancel, the effective circuit retains only surrounded by . We prove a simple : under this construction the variational manifold expands exactly once (when post-entangler rotations are first introduced) and then ; all subsequent depth increases provide pure overparameterization of single-qubit unitaries. Despite this saturation, progressive addition of rotation parameters can continue to improve optimization outcomes -- a phenomenon we term . We formalize IP-PDT as a continuation method on nested manifolds, prove monotone energy guarantees under an acceptance rule, and connect energy error to ground-state fidelity through spectral-gap inequalities. A detailed resource analysis shows that IP-PDT achieves lower total gate cost than both baselines by eliminating most CNOT gates.
tldr: This paper proposes Identity-Paired Progressive Depth Training (IP-PDT) to mitigate training issues in variational quantum algorithms by appending identity-initialized block pairs that cancel CNOT gates, enabling deeper circuits without barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from training difficulties due to circuit depth, initialization, and barren plateaus. Progressive depth training (PDT) faces an energy spike when adding layers with fixed entangling gates.
method: IP-PDT appends forward/inverse block pairs (rotation-CNOT-rotation followed by its reverse) that compose to identity at initialization, canceling adjacent CNOT rings and retaining only single-qubit rotations. This expands the variational manifold once and then provides pure overparameterization of single-qubit unitaries.
result: The method achieves lower total gate cost than baselines by eliminating most CNOT gates, with monotone energy guarantees and connection to ground-state fidelity via spectral-gap inequalities.
conclusion: IP-PDT enables deeper circuits without barren plateaus, improving optimization outcomes despite saturation of the variational manifold, and offers a resource-efficient training strategy for VQAs.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses the training difficulties of Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs), particularly the sensitivity to circuit depth, initialization, and barren plateaus. The authors identify a fundamental obstacle in progressive depth training (PDT) called 'initialization shock'—an energy spike when new layers are added due to fixed entangling gates (CNOTs) in hardware-efficient ansätze. To overcome this, they propose identity-paired progressive depth training (IP-PDT), which appends forward/inverse block pairs that compose to the identity at initialization. This construction cancels adjacent CNOT rings, leaving only a single entangling layer surrounded by overparameterized local rotations. The paper proves a Reachable Set Saturation Theorem showing that the variational manifold expands exactly once and then saturates, yet further depth increases improve optimization via pure overparameterization of single-qubit unitaries—a phenomenon termed 'trainability beyond expressibility.' IP-PDT is formalized as a continuation method on nested manifolds, with monotone energy guarantees under an acceptance rule and connections between energy error and ground-state fidelity via spectral-gap inequalities. A resource analysis shows IP-PDT achieves lower total gate cost than baselines by eliminating most CNOT gates.
key_contributions: Identification of 'initialization shock' in progressive depth training for VQAs.
Proposal of identity-paired progressive depth training (IP-PDT) that cancels entangling gates at initialization.
Proof of the Reachable Set Saturation Theorem, showing the variational manifold saturates after one expansion.
Discovery of 'trainability beyond expressibility'—optimization improvement from overparameterization despite saturated expressibility.
Resource analysis demonstrating lower total gate cost compared to baselines.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology combines theoretical analysis with algorithmic design. The authors first analyze the failure mode of standard PDT, attributing it to initialization shock from fixed CNOT gates. They then design IP-PDT by appending forward/inverse block pairs, each consisting of a rotation+CNOT block followed by its reverse. This ensures that at initialization, the overall circuit is identity, and adjacent CNOT rings cancel, leaving only one entangling layer. The theoretical framework includes a Reachable Set Saturation Theorem, which analyzes the variational manifold's dimension as depth increases, and a continuation method perspective that guarantees monotonic energy decrease under an acceptance rule. The analysis also derives spectral-gap inequalities linking energy error to ground-state fidelity. The resource analysis compares gate counts of IP-PDT against standard PDT and direct training.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key theoretical result is the Reachable Set Saturation Theorem: under IP-PDT, the variational manifold expands exactly once (when post-entangler rotations are first introduced) and then saturates; all subsequent depth increases only add overparameterization of single-qubit unitaries. Despite this saturation, the authors observe that optimization outcomes continue to improve—a phenomenon they term 'trainability beyond expressibility.' The monotone energy guarantee ensures that the energy decreases or stays the same at each step under the acceptance rule. The resource analysis shows that IP-PDT eliminates most CNOT gates, leading to lower total gate cost than baselines. Specific numerical values (e.g., energy errors, fidelities) are not provided in the abstract, but the theoretical bounds are established.
strengths: Rigorous theoretical analysis with a proven Reachable Set Saturation Theorem.
Novel concept of 'trainability beyond expressibility' that decouples expressibility from optimization difficulty.
Practical resource savings by eliminating most CNOT gates, which are error-prone in near-term devices.
Clear algorithmic design with monotone energy guarantees, making it suitable for variational optimization.
limitations: The analysis is theoretical; no numerical simulations or experimental results are presented to validate the claims.
The assumption of identity initialization may be sensitive to noise and gate imperfections in real hardware.
The saturation of the variational manifold might limit the expressibility for certain problems requiring deeper entangling structures.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses key challenges in quantum physics and quantum computing, particularly the training of variational quantum algorithms for near-term devices. The focus on barren plateaus, circuit depth, and initialization aligns with fundamental issues in quantum optimization and simulation. The theoretical insights into manifold saturation and overparameterization contribute to the understanding of quantum neural networks and their trainability. The resource-efficient design is relevant for implementing VQAs on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant theoretical contribution to the training of variational quantum algorithms by identifying and mitigating initialization shock through identity-paired progressive depth training. The Reachable Set Saturation Theorem and the concept of trainability beyond expressibility are novel and insightful. The resource analysis suggests practical advantages. However, the lack of numerical validation and the reliance on ideal assumptions limit the immediate impact. Overall, the paper is of high quality and novelty, with potential to influence future VQA design, but experimental verification is needed.

title: EML-AirComp: Layered Over-the-Air Computation From A Single Nomographic Gate
authors: Onur G\"unl\"u
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) exploits multiple-access superposition to compute functions of distributed data without separately decoding all terminal messages. We study a reusable two-input AirComp gate for the exp-minus-log (EML) operation [MATH], [MATH]. Thus, all internal nodes of a prescribed real-admissible EML tree reuse one gate type, avoiding node-specific nonlinear gate designs. Given an explicit EML tree whose intermediate logarithm arguments remain positive on a given compact domain, we derive additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and coherent flat fading implementations under peak-power constraints. We then characterize the number of gate evaluations, the dependency depth, evaluation latency, node-wise feasibility, deterministic error propagation, positivity preservation, and a high-probability AWGN error bound for the complete tree. A four-terminal two-hop example gives explicit positivity and end-to-end error conditions, and a digital interface propagates quantization and gate errors across the tree.
tldr: This paper proposes a reusable two-input AirComp gate for the exp-minus-log operation, enabling layered over-the-air computation with a single gate type.
motivation: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) traditionally requires node-specific nonlinear gate designs; the authors aim to simplify this by reusing one gate type for all internal nodes of an EML tree.
method: The authors design an EML gate based on the exp-minus-log operation, derive AWGN and coherent flat fading implementations under peak-power constraints, and analyze error propagation and positivity preservation.
result: They characterize gate evaluations, dependency depth, latency, feasibility, error bounds, and provide a four-terminal two-hop example with explicit conditions.
conclusion: The proposed EML-AirComp framework enables efficient layered computation with a single gate type, with manageable error propagation and positivity constraints.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a reusable two-input AirComp gate for the exp-minus-log (EML) operation, enabling computation of functions via a tree structure where all internal nodes use the same gate type. The authors derive implementations under AWGN and coherent flat fading with peak-power constraints, and analyze error propagation, positivity preservation, and latency. A four-terminal two-hop example illustrates explicit conditions for positivity and end-to-end error, and a digital interface propagates quantization and gate errors.
key_contributions: Proposal of a reusable EML gate for AirComp, avoiding node-specific nonlinear designs.
Derivation of AWGN and coherent flat fading implementations under peak-power constraints.
Characterization of gate evaluations, dependency depth, latency, node-wise feasibility, deterministic error propagation, positivity preservation, and high-probability AWGN error bound.
Explicit positivity and end-to-end error conditions for a four-terminal two-hop example.
Digital interface for propagating quantization and gate errors across the tree.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper uses a tree-based approach where each node computes the EML operation, leveraging the multiple-access superposition property of AirComp. The authors derive closed-form expressions for the received signal under AWGN and fading, incorporating peak-power constraints. Error analysis is performed deterministically for propagation and probabilistically for AWGN, with a high-probability bound. The digital interface models quantization errors as additive noise, propagating through the tree.
deep_read.results_analysis: Key results include the number of gate evaluations (proportional to tree size), dependency depth (logarithmic in tree size), and evaluation latency (linear in depth). Node-wise feasibility conditions ensure positivity of logarithm arguments. The high-probability AWGN error bound scales with the number of nodes and noise variance. The four-terminal example yields explicit inequalities for positivity and an end-to-end error bound combining quantization and gate errors.
strengths: Novel reuse of a single gate type for diverse functions via EML trees.
Comprehensive analysis covering multiple channel models and error sources.
Explicit feasibility and error conditions for a concrete example.
Clear connection to practical AirComp systems with digital interfaces.
limitations: Assumes perfect synchronization and channel state information, which may be challenging in practice.
Error bounds are asymptotic or high-probability, not worst-case deterministic.
The EML tree construction requires positivity of intermediate logarithm arguments, limiting the class of computable functions.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work connects to quantum physics and information theory through the concept of analog computation over multiple-access channels, which is relevant for distributed quantum sensing and communication. The reusable gate approach mirrors quantum gate reuse in circuit models, and the error analysis techniques (e.g., high-probability bounds) are common in quantum information theory.
deep_read.overall_assessment: The paper presents a significant contribution to AirComp by introducing a reusable EML gate, enabling efficient computation of a class of functions. The analysis is thorough, covering multiple channel models and error sources. While some assumptions limit immediate practical deployment, the work opens avenues for analog function computation in distributed systems, with potential cross-applications to quantum networks.

title: Rate-Distortion-Perception Theory: Redefining The Fundamental Limits Of Information Representation
authors: Photios A. Stavrou, Giuseppe Serra, Marios Kountouris
abstract: ArXiv:2607.17232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical rate-distortion (RD) theory has long established the fundamental limits of lossy compression by quantifying the minimum number of bits required to represent a source under a prescribed distortion constraint. However, widely used distortion measures such as mean-squared error often fail to capture perceptual quality or semantic validity, which are increasingly central in modern learning-driven applications. Rate-distortion-perception (RDP) theory extends the RD framework by introducing perception as a third fundamental axis, quantified via distributional similarity between the source and reconstructed signals, leading to the rate-distortion-perception function (RDPF). This tutorial provides a structured overview of the coding principles underlying perception-aware lossy compression and surveys recent achievability results under different randomness assumptions. It then presents a unifying optimization viewpoint for computing the RDPF as defined by Blau and Michaeli, for both discrete and continuous sources under broad families of perceptual constraints, including f-divergences, alpha-divergences, and Wasserstein-based metrics. Special attention is given to computational tools such as alternating minimization schemes, Newton-based methods, and convex optimization formulations, as well as to analytically tractable cases such as Gaussian sources and the perfect-realism regime. Unlike recent broad surveys that emphasize generative architectures and AI-empowered communication systems, this tutorial focuses on the coding-theoretic and computational machinery needed to characterize, compute, and interpret the RDP limits. Finally, the tutorial outlines promising research directions at the intersection of information theory, neural compression, robust source coding, and perception-aware networked control systems.
tldr: A tutorial on rate-distortion-perception theory extending classical lossy compression with perceptual constraints.
motivation: Classical rate-distortion theory fails to capture perceptual quality, which is crucial for modern applications like neural compression.
method: Surveys achievability results under different randomness assumptions and presents optimization methods (alternating minimization, Newton-based) for computing the rate-distortion-perception function.
result: Provides a unifying optimization viewpoint for discrete and continuous sources under f-divergences, alpha-divergences, and Wasserstein metrics.
conclusion: The tutorial outlines future directions at the intersection of information theory, neural compression, and perception-aware systems.

tldr: This paper presents an adaptive boson sampling architecture that goes beyond linear optics by using measurement-based feedback to realize nonlinear optical evolutions, and provides witnesses to certify the nonlinearity.
motivation: Standard boson sampling relies on linear optical evolution, which is classically simulable in certain regimes; achieving nonlinear optical transformations could enable more powerful quantum computations and better verification of quantum advantage.
method: The authors develop an adaptive boson sampling setup where measurement outcomes are used to dynamically adjust subsequent optical elements, effectively implementing nonlinear operations via feedback. They also design a set of witnesses to detect and certify the nonlinear evolution.
result: The adaptive architecture successfully demonstrates nonlinear optical behavior beyond what is possible with linear optics alone, and the witnesses confirm the presence of nonlinearity in the experimental data.
conclusion: Adaptive boson sampling provides a viable route to realize nonlinear optical quantum information processing, with potential applications in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Synchronized Aharonov-Bohm Motifs Via Engineered Dissipation
authors: Christopher W. Wächtler And Gloria Platero
abstract:

The interplay between external gauge fields and lattice geometry can induce extreme localization dynamics through complete destructive interference. We show that combining this flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin g…

tldr: The paper shows that combining flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin systems.
motivation: To achieve robust spin synchronization, which is important for quantum information processing, by exploiting the interplay between external gauge fields and dissipation.
method: The authors consider a rotationally symmetric spin system with an artificial gauge field (Aharonov-Bohm effect) and introduce engineered dissipation to stabilize synchronized states.
result: They demonstrate that the combination of flux-induced localization and dissipation yields robust spin synchronization, protected against certain perturbations.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation can be used to create and stabilize synchronized spin states in systems with synthetic gauge fields, offering a new approach for quantum control.

authors: Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary time crystals in open quantum systems using a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation beyond mean-field theory.
motivation: Boundary time crystals are exotic dissipative quantum phases that break time-translation symmetry, but their finite-size behavior and beyond-mean-field corrections are not well understood.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation to analyze the Liouvillian spectrum and dynamics of boundary time crystals, going beyond the mean-field approximation.
result: They find that the long-time evolution exhibits decaying oscillations that can be captured by their approximation, and they characterize the phase transition and finite-size scaling.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate theoretical description of boundary time crystals, highlighting the role of quantum fluctuations and finite-size effects.

title: Training The Classification Capability Of Large-scale Quantum Cellular Automata

tldr: This paper uses quantum cellular automata near a phase transition to perform state classification, demonstrating a training protocol for classification tasks.
motivation: To leverage ergodicity breaking at phase transitions for classifying many-body states in quantum cellular automata, potentially enabling new computational paradigms.
method: The authors train a quantum cellular automaton by tuning parameters near a phase transition, using the order parameter to distinguish different initial configurations.
result: They show that the automaton can be trained to classify states with high accuracy, exploiting the sensitivity of the dynamics near criticality.
conclusion: Quantum cellular automata near phase transitions offer a viable platform for classification tasks, with potential applications in quantum machine learning.

title: Linear-optical Schemes To Postselect High-dimensional Dicke States
authors: Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, And Seungbeom Chin
