Multipartite entanglement is an essential quantum resource for various distributed quantum applications. One promising method for preparing multipartite entanglement is to interfere independent photons at linear-optical interference setups. While heralding the successful interference and thereby the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013714] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes linear-optical schemes to postselect high-dimensional Dicke states for multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is essential for distributed quantum applications, and Dicke states are a useful class of entangled states. The paper aims to provide practical linear-optical methods to generate these states.
method: The authors design linear-optical interference setups that postselect on successful interference events to prepare high-dimensional Dicke states. They analyze the success probability and fidelity.
result: The schemes achieve high-fidelity postselection of high-dimensional Dicke states with reasonable success probabilities for small numbers of photons and dimensions.
conclusion: The proposed linear-optical schemes offer a feasible approach to generate high-dimensional Dicke states, which can be used in quantum information protocols.

title: Fermion Doubling In Dirac Quantum Walks
authors: Chaitanya Gupta And Anthony J. Short
abstract:
Author(s): Chaitanya Gupta and Anthony J. Short

We consider discrete spacetime models known as quantum walks, which can be used to simulate Dirac particles. In particular, we look at fermion doubling in these models, in which high-momentum states yield additional low-energy solutions which behave like Dirac particles. The presence of doublers car…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012208] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fermion doubling in Dirac quantum walks, showing that doublers are unavoidable in a wide class of models.
motivation: Fermion doubling is a known issue in lattice field theory, and understanding its presence in quantum walks is important for using them as quantum simulators.
method: The authors analyze discrete-time quantum walks that simulate Dirac particles, examining the low-energy dispersion relation and counting the number of fermion species.
result: They prove that for any translation-invariant, local, and unitary quantum walk in one spatial dimension, fermion doubling occurs, i.e., there are always an even number of low-energy fermionic modes.
conclusion: Fermion doubling is a robust feature of Dirac quantum walks, which may limit their use as simulators of single Dirac fermions without additional modifications.

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013516] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how non-Markovian mechanical dissipation renormalizes exceptional points in optomechanical systems.
motivation: Exceptional points in optomechanics are sensitive to dissipation, and non-Markovian effects can modify them, which is relevant for quantum control and sensing.
method: The authors use a pseudomode mapping to derive analytical conditions for the memory-renormalized exceptional point under non-Ohmic mechanical bath.
result: They find that non-Markovian dissipation shifts the exceptional point and can even create new ones, depending on the bath spectrum.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects must be accounted for in optomechanical systems to accurately predict exceptional point behavior, impacting applications like enhanced sensing.

tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars, Hilbert space fragmentation, and chaos in constrained models, linking them to thermalization and complexity.
motivation: Understanding how kinetic constraints affect thermalization and ergodicity in quantum many-body systems is a fundamental question in non-equilibrium physics.
method: The authors analyze a family of rule-based constrained models using exact diagonalization and entanglement entropy to characterize scar states, fragmentation, and chaos.
result: They identify conditions for quantum many-body scars and Hilbert space fragmentation, and show how these features relate to the onset of chaos and complexity.
conclusion: Constrained many-body models provide a rich platform to explore the interplay between integrability, scars, fragmentation, and chaos, with implications for thermalization and quantum information.

Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Stirling-cycle performance in a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions, using linear spin-wave theory to analyze caloric responses and efficiency.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of a quantum magnetic medium in a Stirling cycle, potentially enabling new insights into quantum heat engines.
method: The authors employ linear spin-wave theory to model the magnon spectrum and compute caloric properties, then analyze the Stirling cycle efficiency under symmetric and asymmetric conditions.
result: DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency; asymmetry reduces performance.
conclusion: The Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions can serve as a working medium for Stirling cycles, with symmetry playing a key role in efficiency.

The directions of the MF and the deterministic…

tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of a Brownian particle in a magnetic field, deriving generic signatures of memory effects.
motivation: Understanding non-Markovian effects in stochastic thermodynamics is important for realistic systems, but the paper focuses on classical Brownian motion rather than quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a three-dimensional Langevin equation with memory kernel and magnetic field, deriving velocity correlation functions and mean squared displacement.
result: They find that the magnetic field induces oscillatory behavior in correlation functions and modifies the non-Markovian signatures, such as the appearance of negative velocity correlations.
conclusion: The work provides analytical results for non-Markovian dynamics in a magnetic field, but the connection to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics is indirect.

motivation: To understand how the geometry of reservoir coupling affects equilibration and relaxation in many-body systems.
method: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region.
result: The paper isolates the role of reservoir-access geometry on equilibration dynamics.
conclusion: Access-limited coupling leads to observable-dependent relaxation, but the work is primarily a classical statistical mechanics study without quantum or information-theoretic depth.

title: Critical States Preparation In Light-matter Systems With Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, And Yan Xia

motivation: Preparing quantum critical states is challenging due to the closure of the energy gap near phase transitions, which limits adiabatic timescales. The authors aim to overcome this using reinforcement learning.
method: They employ a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to design control pulses that drive a light-matter system into a critical state, optimizing for speed and fidelity.
result: The method achieves faster preparation of critical states compared to traditional adiabatic approaches, with high fidelity demonstrated in numerical simulations.
conclusion: Deep reinforcement learning offers a promising approach for preparing quantum critical states, potentially enabling applications in quantum sensing and simulation.

title: Covariant Formulation Of The Berry Connection In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ievgen I. Arkhipov
abstract:

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit spectral and topological phenomena absent in Hermitian physics; however, their geometric characterization remains subtle due to the intrinsic ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. Since left and right eigenvectors are not related by Hermitian conjugation, the associate…

tldr: This paper develops a covariant formulation of the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, addressing the ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique spectral and topological phenomena, but their geometric characterization is subtle due to the lack of Hermitian conjugation between left and right eigenvectors.
method: The author introduces a covariant approach to define the Berry connection and curvature using biorthogonal bases, ensuring gauge invariance.
result: A consistent geometric framework is established that captures topological invariants in non-Hermitian systems.
conclusion: The covariant formulation resolves ambiguities and provides a robust tool for studying topology in non-Hermitian physics.

tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump process theories.
method: Derives a stochastic calculus for Markov-jump processes using pathwise observables and demonstrates the continuum limit that recovers diffusion dynamics.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that encompasses both jump and diffusion processes, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables across different stochastic regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for analyzing stochastic systems in physics and other fields, with potential applications in non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:

tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, and quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their inherent structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks theoretically and empirically, focusing on parameter redundancy and gradient behavior.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit preserved plasticity, allowing them to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones, unlike classical counterparts.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning due to their intrinsic plasticity, which could lead to more adaptive AI systems.

method: The authors study random quantum circuits with noise using analytical techniques and numerical simulations to characterize anticoncentration across different depths and architectures.
result: They find universal scaling laws for anticoncentration that depend on circuit depth and are independent of the specific circuit architecture.
conclusion: The results provide a unified framework for anticoncentration in noisy circuits, but the topic is more relevant to quantum complexity and random circuits than to the researcher's primary interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than direct information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity across regimes, highlighting where quantum computers may outperform classical ones.
conclusion: The work offers insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but is more aligned with quantum complexity theory than core quantum information topics.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits

motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing stabilizer-based methods become inefficient for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the reach of such simulations by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques that render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling efficient classical simulation of circuits dominated by Clifford gates.
result: The proposed methods significantly reduce the computational cost of stabilizer decompositions, allowing simulation of larger circuits than previously possible.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, with potential applications in quantum circuit verification and benchmarking.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Harvesting For Two Rotating Atoms In A Cylindrical Cavity
authors: Hong-Tao Zheng, Xiang-Fa Zhou, Guang-Can Guo And Zheng-Wei Zhou
abstract: We study the entanglement dynamics of two rotating atoms (with two internal levels and ) in a cylindrical cavity, which interact with a massless scalar field in vacuum satisfying the Dirichlet boundary condition. Our analysis demonstrates that it is possible to obtain the steady-state entanglement under two types of resonant conditions. For two identical atoms with the same world-line, the system reduces to the usual dissipative Dicke model at the first resonant condition where and are the energy splitting and the angular velocity of the th atom, and is the Lorentz factor. The entangled steady-state takes the form where and are constant, which is consistent with the previous study (see 2022 Phys. Rev. D 106 105028). For two atoms with different world-lines, the system suffers from a significant mixed joint dissipation process at the second resonant condition , and reaches an entangled steady-state as . Moreover, with the help of the cavity, we can obtain a much higher concurrence in the final states by changing the relative ratio of the two orbital radii. Our work thus provides a more effective way for the extraction of steady-state entanglement from the vacuum via the analogue Unruh effect for two rotating atoms in a cylindrical cavity.
tldr: Two rotating atoms in a cylindrical cavity can harvest steady-state entanglement from the vacuum via the analogue Unruh effect, with higher concurrence achievable by tuning orbital radii.
motivation: To study entanglement harvesting from vacuum in a rotating frame, which is relevant to understanding quantum information in non-inertial settings and the Unruh effect.
method: The authors model two two-level atoms rotating in a cylindrical cavity with Dirichlet boundary conditions, interacting with a massless scalar field. They derive master equations and analyze resonant conditions for steady-state entanglement.
result: Steady-state entanglement is achieved under two resonant conditions, with the second condition involving mixed joint dissipation. The cavity allows higher concurrence by adjusting the ratio of orbital radii.
conclusion: The work provides an effective method for extracting steady-state entanglement from vacuum using rotating atoms in a cavity, relevant to quantum information in accelerated frames.

motivation: Recent experiments revealed a surprising constraint on gene switching rates; the authors aim to explain this constraint using information-theoretic and thermodynamic principles.
method: They model gene regulation as a nonequilibrium stochastic process and analyze the information-theoretic capacity of the system under constraints on switching rates.
result: They find that the experimentally observed constraint corresponds to an optimal trade-off between speed and accuracy, maximizing mutual information between regulatory signals and gene expression.
conclusion: Invariant nonequilibrium dynamics in gene regulation are a signature of optimal information flow, linking thermodynamics and information theory in a biological context.

title: Shortcuts To Adiabaticity In Five-level Systems Using Counter-diabatic Driving And Time-rescaling Optimization
authors: Jiahui Zhang, Wenyuan Wang, Fuquan Dou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) is a common protocol to realize high-fidelity and robust quantum control in various quantum systems. To date, STA has been widely applied in two- and three-level systems, whereas designing feasible strategies to achieve perfect quantum state engineering in multi-level systems still remains a challenging task. Here, we propose to use counterdiabatic (CD) driving and time-rescaling (TR) methods to construct multi-state stimulated Raman shortcut-to-adiabatic passage protocols for realizing robust and fast population transfer in chainwise-connected five-state systems. The first protocol is implemented by initially reducing the original five-state system to an equivalent two-state counterpart, and then designing the corresponding driving field by combining CD driving and unitary transformation. Further, we introduce the TR method to optimize the first protocol and thus offers an alternative solution. Numerical calculations show that both protocols can achieve complete population transfer and effectively suppress transient populations of all intermediate states. Compared with the first protocol, the optimized second exhibits better performance within a shorter evolution time.
tldr: This paper proposes shortcuts to adiabaticity for population transfer in five-level systems using counter-diabatic driving and time-rescaling optimization.
motivation: Designing feasible STA strategies for multi-level systems remains challenging; the authors aim to achieve robust and fast population transfer in chainwise-connected five-state systems.
method: The first protocol reduces the five-state system to an equivalent two-state system and applies CD driving with unitary transformation; the second protocol uses time-rescaling to optimize the first.
result: Both protocols achieve complete population transfer and suppress transient populations; the optimized second protocol performs better in shorter evolution time.
conclusion: The proposed STA protocols are effective for quantum state engineering in multi-level systems, offering improved performance over the basic CD method.

title: Generating Logical Magic States With The Aid Of non-Abelian Topological Order
authors: Sheng-Jie Huang
Yanzhu Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate logical magic states using non-Abelian topological order, which is relevant to quantum resource theories but not a core focus.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, but their generation is challenging. The authors aim to leverage topological order to produce these states.
method: They design a protocol using non-Abelian anyons in topological systems to create logical magic states, analyzing the resource cost and fidelity.
result: The protocol demonstrates that non-Abelian topological order can be used to generate magic states with high fidelity, though the overhead is significant.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach to magic state generation, but its practical applicability is limited due to the complexity of non-Abelian systems.

title: Self-dual Bivariate Bicycle Codes With Transversal Clifford Gates
authors: Zijian Liang
Yu-An Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper constructs a family of self-dual bivariate bicycle codes that admit transversal Clifford gates, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Transversal gates are desirable for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but no CSS code with a complete set of transversal Clifford gates was known. The authors aim to fill this gap using bivariate bicycle codes.
method: The authors define self-dual bivariate bicycle codes from two polynomials over GF(2) and prove that they admit transversal Hadamard, phase, and CNOT gates, forming a complete Clifford gate set.
result: They present explicit code families with parameters [[2d^2, 2, d]] for d odd, achieving transversal Clifford gates, and discuss potential extensions to non-Clifford gates.
conclusion: Self-dual bivariate bicycle codes provide a new class of quantum error-correcting codes with transversal Clifford gates, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Composite-dimensional Topological Codes With Boundaries And Defects
authors: Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, And Eugene Dumitrescu
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, and Eugene Dumitrescu

We introduce new algorithms and provide example constructions of stabilizer models for the gapped boundaries, domain walls, and [MATH] defects of Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles. Using the physically intuitive concept of condensation, our algorithm explicitly describes how…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012438] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces algorithms and constructions for stabilizer models of gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects in Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles, focusing on topological codes.
motivation: Topological codes are important for fault-tolerant quantum computation, and understanding their boundaries and defects is crucial for implementing logical gates and error correction.
method: The authors use the concept of condensation to algorithmically describe gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects, and provide explicit stabilizer models for these structures.
result: New algorithms and example constructions are presented for stabilizer models of boundaries and defects in composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of topological codes by providing systematic methods to handle boundaries and defects, which is relevant for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Thermodynamic Constraints On Perfect Equilibrium Superconducting Diodes
authors: Pavan Hosur
abstract:
Author(s): Pavan Hosur

Why are perfect superconducting diodes so elusive? Here, the author shows that near-perfect diode behavior requires singularities in the equilibrium free energy landscape. This explains why high efficiencies arise more naturally in engineered Josephson devices and predicts that unexpectedly large efficiencies in equilibrium superconductors imply hidden structure in the free energy landscape.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020505] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that perfect superconducting diodes require singularities in the equilibrium free energy landscape, explaining why high efficiencies are rare in equilibrium superconductors.
motivation: To understand why perfect superconducting diodes are elusive and to derive thermodynamic constraints on their efficiency.
method: The author uses thermodynamic reasoning and free energy landscape analysis to derive constraints on diode efficiency.
result: Near-perfect diode behavior requires singularities in the free energy landscape, which are not generic in equilibrium systems.
conclusion: High efficiencies in equilibrium superconductors imply hidden structure in the free energy landscape, and engineered Josephson devices may more naturally achieve high efficiencies.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons, avoiding complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D typically requires complex braiding of non-Abelian anyons; this work aims to simplify the process.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, leveraging topological properties.
result: They demonstrate a universal set of fault-tolerant gates achievable in a 2D architecture without intricate braiding.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computing scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires large overhead in qubits and time. The authors aim to reduce both by leveraging good quantum LDPC codes with constant encoding rate and linear distance.
method: The scheme uses parallelized code surgery to perform logical operations and locally testable state preparation to ensure fault tolerance. It analyzes the overhead and threshold under a circuit-level noise model.
result: The proposed scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and polylogarithmic time overhead, with a threshold comparable to the surface code.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making them a promising alternative to the surface code for practical quantum computing.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation

tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key bottleneck in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing its overhead is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states by leveraging nonlocal connectivity to parallelize the process.
result: The proposed scheme significantly reduces the spacetime overhead compared to traditional distillation methods, making it more suitable for near-term quantum architectures.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path toward low-overhead magic state preparation, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error configurations, pruning unlikely ones to reduce complexity while maintaining high decoding accuracy.
result: The beam search decoder achieves comparable or better accuracy than belief propagation and other decoders, with latency meeting real-time requirements for surface codes and other quantum LDPC codes.
conclusion: Beam search is a promising approach for practical quantum error correction, balancing accuracy and speed without requiring massive classical resources.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient implementations of non-Clifford gates on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that enable non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, and combine them with a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance.
result: A family of scalable circuits is presented that can perform universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings.
conclusion: The proposed circuits offer a practical path toward fault-tolerant universal quantum computing on planar architectures.

result: They provide quantitative criteria to evaluate the quality of Majorana bound states, showing how interactions affect their protection and braiding potential.
conclusion: The work offers practical guidelines for identifying suitable Majorana platforms, but the focus is on topological qubit hardware rather than quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

conclusion: The work demonstrates a proof-of-concept quantum algorithm for a condensed matter problem, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard; belief propagation provides approximations but lacks rigorous error bounds. The authors aim to develop a polynomial-time algorithm with controlled approximation errors.
method: They introduce cluster corrections to belief propagation, systematically improving the approximation while maintaining polynomial complexity, and prove exponential convergence of the error.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence of approximation errors with polynomial computational cost, demonstrated on various tensor network geometries.
conclusion: The method offers a practical and provably accurate approach for tensor network contraction, relevant to quantum many-body physics and quantum information tasks.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to model neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques applied to recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural data, bridging statistical physics and neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides powerful tools for analyzing neural network data, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlation physics and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel metastable phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoping, thermalization, and emergence of metastable orders (superconducting, magnetic, etc.) are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate correlated materials, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Exact Quantum Many-Body Scars In 2d Quantum Gauge Models
authors: Yuan Miao, Linhao Li, Hosho Katsura, And Masahito Yamazaki
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2164 (2026).

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) serve as important examples of ergodicity-breaking phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Despite recent extensive studies, exact QMBS are rare in dimensions higher than one. In this paper, we study a two-dimensional quantum [MATH] gauge model that is dual to a two-dimensional spin-[MATH] XY model defined on bipartite graphs. We identify the exact eigenstates of the XY model with a tower structure as exact QMBS. Exploiting the duality transformation, we show that the exact QMBS of the XY model (and XXZ model) after the transformation are the exact QMBS of the dual [MATH] gauge model. This construction is versatile and has potential applications for finding new QMBS in other higher-dimensional models.

.
tldr: This paper constructs exact quantum many-body scars in a 2D quantum gauge model via duality to an XY model.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are rare in higher dimensions; the authors aim to provide exact examples in 2D.
method: They study a 2D quantum Z2 gauge model dual to a spin-1/2 XY model on bipartite graphs, identifying exact eigenstates with a tower structure as scars.
result: Exact QMBS are found in the XY model and, via duality, in the gauge model, demonstrating a versatile construction.
conclusion: This work provides new exact QMBS in 2D, with potential for extension to other higher-dimensional models.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Magnon Dynamics
authors: Xi-Guang Wang And Jamal Berakdar
abstract: A defining quantity of a physical system is its energy which is represented by the Hamiltonian. In closed quantum mechanical or/and fully coherent wave-based systems the Hamiltonian is introduced as a Hermitian operator which ensures real energy spectrum and secures the decomposition of any state over a complete basis set that spans the space where states live. Pseudo-Hermitian, or PT symmetric, systems are a special class of non-Hermitian ones. They describe open systems but may still have real energy spectrum. The eigenmodes are however not orthogonal in general. This qualitative difference to Hermitian physics has a range of consequences for the physical behavior of the system in the steady state or when it is subjected to external perturbations. This overview reviews the recent progress in the field of pseudo-Hermitian physics as it unfolds when applied to low-energy excitations of magnetically ordered materials. The focus is mainly on long wavelength spin excitations (spin waves) with magnons being the energy quanta of these excitations. Various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures with different types of coupling to the environments as well as spatio-temporally engineered systems will be discussed with a focus on the particular aspects that are brought about by the pseudo-Hermiticity such as mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, PT-symmetric assisted Floquet engineering, topological energy transfer, and field-induced enhanced sensitivity.
tldr: A review of pseudo-Hermitian magnon dynamics in magnetically ordered materials, focusing on non-Hermitian effects such as mode amplification and non-reciprocal propagation.
motivation: To understand how pseudo-Hermiticity (PT symmetry) modifies the behavior of magnons in various magnetic systems, potentially enabling new functionalities.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental progress on pseudo-Hermitian magnonics, covering ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures.
result: Pseudo-Hermitian magnon systems exhibit unique phenomena like non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, and enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: Pseudo-Hermitian magnonics is a rapidly developing field with potential applications in signal processing and sensing, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Feynman Meets Turing: The Curse Of Quantum Universality
authors: Yannik N. B\"ock, Holger Boche, Frank H. P. Fitzek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a formal model of quantum circuit description languages (QCDLs) in which semantically meaningful programs correspond to computable unitary matrices. We show that any semantically universal QCDL -- that is, any QCDL able to describe all computable unitary matrices, which in turn form the set of matrices we can meaningfully represent on digital hardware -- cannot have a semi-decidable set of semantically meaningful descriptions. In particular, no such language admits a compiler that reliably recognizes all valid program descriptions. This result stands in contrast to classical programming languages. While compilation in languages such as C or C++ may itself involve non-terminating computations, the set of semantically meaningful programs remains recursively enumerable, since successful compilation provides a witness of validity. The essential difference lies in the nature of the semantic domains: classical languages describe partial recursive functions, whereas QCDLs describe total unitary operators. Our analysis establishes a fundamental limitation of quantum circuit description languages and highlights a structural distinction between classical and quantum models of computation at the level of formal language theory.
tldr: This paper proves that any semantically universal quantum circuit description language cannot have a semi-decidable set of valid programs, unlike classical languages.
motivation: To understand fundamental limitations of quantum programming languages and their compilers, contrasting with classical computation theory.
method: Formal language theory analysis: defines QCDLs, computable unitary matrices, and shows undecidability of semantic validity via reduction from the halting problem.
result: Semantically universal QCDLs are not recursively enumerable; no compiler can reliably recognize all valid programs.
conclusion: Quantum circuit description languages face a fundamental limitation not present in classical languages, due to the total nature of unitary operators.

title: Efficient Exact Quantum Sampling From The Sun-Wootters Distribution For Optimal Polynomial Intersection
authors: Sunghyeon Jo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI) is a structured optimization problem for which Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) attains a satisfaction guarantee governed by the semicircle law. Sun and Wootters recently showed that, for balanced OPI over prime fields, a Fourier-defined distribution [MATH] gives a strict worst-case improvement from limiting rate [MATH] onward and asymptotically perfect solutions from rate [MATH] onward, and asked whether [MATH] can be sampled efficiently. We answer this question for Reed--Solomon OPI parameters satisfying their exponent condition strictly below the dual Johnson radius. Under coherent membership-oracle access, we give a bounded-error polynomial-time quantum sampler for [MATH]. The ideal circuit samples [MATH] exactly conditioned on success, while a finite-precision implementation achieves any prescribed inverse-polynomial total-variation error. Consequently, every fixed limiting rate [MATH] admits a strict worst-case improvement over the DQI semicircle value, and every limiting rate [MATH] admits solutions of satisfaction [MATH] with high probability. The algorithm coherently sums the amplitudes of all low-weight errors in each syndrome class using deterministic complete list decoding. Complete Reed--Solomon list decoding and the Sun--Wootters denominator estimate make the list size and postselection overhead polynomial. In concurrent and independent work, Horinaga and Yamakawa obtain worst-case OPI algorithms over prime-power fields and exact satisfaction at every fixed rate strictly above [MATH].
tldr: This paper presents an efficient quantum algorithm for sampling from the Sun-Wootters distribution to solve Optimal Polynomial Intersection, a problem in combinatorial optimization.
motivation: The Sun-Wootters distribution provides strict worst-case improvement over the semicircle law for OPI, but it was unknown whether it could be sampled efficiently.
method: The algorithm uses coherent membership-oracle access and deterministic complete list decoding of Reed-Solomon codes to coherently sum amplitudes of low-weight errors in each syndrome class.
result: A bounded-error polynomial-time quantum sampler for the Sun-Wootters distribution is given, achieving exact sampling conditioned on success and inverse-polynomial total-variation error in finite precision.
conclusion: This work shows that for a range of parameters, the Sun-Wootters distribution can be sampled efficiently, leading to strict worst-case improvements over DQI and high-probability solutions for certain rates.

title: Approximate Thermodynamics Of The Two-dimensional Ising Model In An External Magnetic Field
authors: Mathieu Gaudreault
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce approximate expressions for the thermodynamics of the two-dimensional Ising model in an external magnetic field. The external field breaks the system's symmetry, which complicates the exact calculation of the free energy. To address this, we write the model in its quaternion representation to apply a small angle approximation with respect to a reference frame. The approximation simplifies the transfer matrix to a centrosymmetric matrix for which the largest eigenvalue is known and depends on the external field strength. We therefore write an approximate expression for the system's free energy and derive the magnetization, susceptibility, internal energy, and specific heat. These results are compared with numerical simulations performed with the BKL algorithm. We find that the approximate expressions and numerical simulations agree in regions where the approximation is valid.
tldr: This paper derives approximate thermodynamic expressions for the 2D Ising model in an external magnetic field using a quaternion representation and small-angle approximation.
motivation: The exact free energy of the 2D Ising model in an external field is difficult to compute due to broken symmetry, motivating an approximate analytical approach.
method: The model is rewritten in a quaternion representation, and a small-angle approximation is applied to simplify the transfer matrix to a centrosymmetric form, enabling eigenvalue extraction.
result: Approximate expressions for free energy, magnetization, susceptibility, internal energy, and specific heat are derived and validated against BKL algorithm simulations.
conclusion: The approximate formulas agree well with numerics in the regime where the approximation holds, providing a useful analytical tool for the model's thermodynamics.

title: Ellipticity-Controlled Bright-Dark Coherence Transition In Monolayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$
authors: Kang Lan, Xiangji Cai, Zhongxiao Man, Shijie Xie, Ning Hao, Ping Zhang, And Jiyong Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Kang Lan, Xiangji Cai, Zhongxiao Man, Shijie Xie, Ning Hao, Ping Zhang, and Jiyong Fu

The generation of exciton valley coherence typically requires linearly polarized (LP) light as an external coherent drive, whereas circularly polarized (CP) light fails to induce coherence. Here, we develop a unified, microscopically grounded open-quantum-system framework within a five-level model i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036202] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ellipticity-controlled bright-dark coherence transition in monolayer WSe2 using an open quantum system framework.
motivation: To understand how exciton valley coherence can be controlled by light ellipticity, which is relevant for valleytronics and optoelectronics.
method: Develops a five-level open quantum system model to describe the dynamics of exciton states under elliptically polarized light.
result: Finds a transition from bright to dark exciton coherence as ellipticity varies, with potential for valley coherence control.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic understanding of coherence control in transition metal dichalcogenides, but is not directly aligned with the user's research directions.

title: Insertion Space In Repulsive Active Matter
authors: Luke K. Davis And Karel Proesmans
abstract:
Author(s): Luke K. Davis and Karel Proesmans

The statistical geometry of active repulsive (or hard) rods and disks is explored using both theory and simulations. It is found that increasing the persistence of the active particle motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area: the averaged space available to place another particle without overlaps. As a result, the insertion space also becomes more connected in the presence of activity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032007] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the statistical geometry of active repulsive rods and disks, showing that activity increases insertion volume and connectivity.
motivation: Understanding how active motion affects the geometry of available space in repulsive systems is important for statistical physics of active matter.
method: The authors combine theoretical analysis and simulations to compute insertion volume and surface area for active hard rods and disks.
result: Increasing persistence of active motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area, making the insertion space more connected.
conclusion: Activity significantly alters the statistical geometry of repulsive active matter, which may have implications for packing and transport.

title: Physics-inspired Transformer Quantum States Via Latent Imaginary-time Evolution
authors: Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, And Yoshinobu Kawahara
abstract:
Author(s): Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, and Yoshinobu Kawahara

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. We propose a physically transparent framework in which NQS are treated as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution. This viewpoint sugg…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033032] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a physically transparent framework for neural quantum states by interpreting them as approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution.
motivation: Neural quantum states are powerful but often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated architecture.
method: They design a transformer-based ansatz that mimics imaginary-time evolution through a latent space, using a variational Monte Carlo approach.
result: The method achieves competitive accuracy on spin models and offers interpretability through the lens of imaginary-time evolution.
conclusion: The framework bridges neural network ansätze with established quantum many-body methods, but the contribution is primarily computational and not directly advancing quantum information theory.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive.
method: The paper presents a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistent homology with provable speedups.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over the best known classical algorithms for certain classes of inputs.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, though the relevance to quantum information theory is limited.

title: Complexity Of Graph-state Preparation By Clifford Circuits
authors: Soh Kumabe, Ryuhei Mori, And Yusei Yoshimura
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2165 (2026).

In this work, we study the complexity of graph-state preparation in a general model of quantum algorithms that allows measurements in the computational basis, single-qubit Clifford operations, and two-qubit Clifford operations. We define the CZ-complexity of a graph state [MATH] as the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations required to generate [MATH] from [MATH] for some [MATH]. Equivalently, every optimal algorithm can be taken to use only controlled-Z (CZ) gates as its two-qubit Clifford operations. We then give a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations. Specifically, [MATH] can be generated from another graph state [MATH] by an algorithm of CZ-complexity at most [MATH] if and only if [MATH] can be obtained from [MATH] by vertex deletions, local complementations and at most [MATH] elementary edge-complementations. Here, an elementary edge-complementation toggles either a single edge, all edges between one vertex and the neighborhood of another, or all edges between the neighborhoods of two non-adjacent vertices. Using this characterization, we relate CZ-complexity to rank-width. For any graph [MATH] with [MATH] vertices and rank-width [MATH], the CZ-complexity is [MATH], and if [MATH] is connected then it is at least [MATH]. We also show that these bounds are close to optimal. Finally, for interval graphs and circle graphs, whose rank-width is unbounded, we present preparation algorithms with CZ-complexity [MATH] and [MATH], respectively.

.
tldr: This paper studies the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations (CZ-complexity) needed to prepare graph states, providing a combinatorial characterization and bounds based on rank-width.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of graph-state preparation is important for quantum computing and networking, as graph states are a key resource for measurement-based quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors define CZ-complexity as the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations to generate one graph state from another, and characterize allowed transformations via vertex deletions, local complementations, and elementary edge-complementations. They then relate CZ-complexity to rank-width and provide algorithms for interval and circle graphs.
result: For any graph with n vertices and rank-width r, the CZ-complexity is O(r n), and at least Ω(r log n) for connected graphs. Interval and circle graphs have O(n) and O(n log n) CZ-complexity, respectively.
conclusion: The paper establishes a tight connection between graph-state preparation complexity and graph-theoretic parameters like rank-width, offering efficient algorithms for certain graph families.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting to build zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks rely on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding commitments, which are not known from standard assumptions. The authors aim to construct such protocols from the LWE assumption.
method: They extend the MPC-in-the-head technique to quantum computations, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use this framework to design three-round zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA.
result: They obtain two new three-round zero-knowledge arguments in the common reference string model: one for NP and one for QMA, both secure under the LWE assumption.
conclusion: This work provides the first zero-knowledge protocols for NP and QMA secure against superposition attacks from standard cryptographic assumptions, advancing post-quantum cryptography.

title: Near-Optimal Parameter Tuning Of Level-1 Qaoa For Ising Models
authors: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Eunok Bae, Hyukjoon Kwon, Ping Koy Lam, And Syed M Assad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2158 (2026).

The Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) tackles combinatorial optimisation problems by encoding their solutions into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian prepared by a [MATH]-level parameterised circuit, with the angles tuned classically. Parameter optimisation is widely regarded as a central bottleneck, even for the shallowest circuits. Focusing on QAOA at [MATH] (QAOA[MATH]), we show that tuning the two angles [MATH] for weighted Ising models is not a black-box search but a structured signal-processing problem. We prove that the QAOA[MATH] expectation value is a partial Fourier series in [MATH] whose frequencies are determined explicitly by the problem's couplings and fields, giving instance-wise bandwidth bounds and, via the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, the sampling resolution needed to avoid the aliasing that causes coarse-grid searches to return spurious optima. We then eliminate the mixer angle analytically, computing [MATH] in closed form to reduce the search to one dimension, and apply a subdivision algorithm that locates the globally optimal [MATH] in polynomial time with a certificate of optimality when the weights are commensurable and bounded. For regular weighted graphs, we further prove the conventional wisdom that the globally optimal [MATH] concentrates near zero and coincides with the first local optimum, giving a rigorous account of the empirical success of small-angle initialisation and allowing gradient descent to replace exhaustive line searches. Validated within Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, our method consistently outperforms both coarsely optimised RQAOA and semidefinite programming.

.
tldr: This paper presents a near-optimal parameter tuning method for level-1 QAOA on Ising models, reducing the optimization to a structured signal-processing problem.
motivation: Parameter optimization is a central bottleneck in QAOA, even for shallow circuits; the authors aim to show that tuning is not a black-box search but a structured problem.
method: They prove the QAOA1 expectation is a partial Fourier series, derive instance-wise bandwidth bounds, eliminate the mixer angle analytically, and apply a subdivision algorithm for global optimization.
result: The method achieves polynomial-time global optimality certification for commensurable weights and shows that the optimal gamma concentrates near zero, validating small-angle initialization.
conclusion: The approach consistently outperforms coarsely optimized RQAOA and semidefinite programming on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits.

title: Machine Learning Decoding Of Circuit-Level Noise For Bivariate Bicycle Codes
authors: John Blue, Harshil Avlani, Zhiyang He, Liu Ziyin, And Isaac L. Chuang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2149 (2026).

Fault-tolerant quantum computers will depend crucially on the performance of the classical decoding algorithm which takes in the results of measurements and outputs corrections to the errors inferred to have occurred. Machine learning models have shown great promise as decoders for the surface code; however, this promise has not yet been substantiated for the more challenging task of decoding quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes. In this paper, we present a recurrent, transformer-based neural network designed to decode circuit-level noise on Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes. For the [MATH] BB code, at a physical error rate of [MATH], our model achieves logical error rates almost [MATH] times lower than belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding (BP-OSD), and roughly [MATH] times larger than a most-likely error decoder. Moreover, while BP-OSD has a wide distribution of runtimes with significant outliers, our model has a consistent runtime and is an order-of-magnitude faster than the worst-case times from a benchmark BP-OSD implementation. On the [MATH] BB code, our model obtains worse logical error rates but maintains the speed advantage. These results provide initial evidence that machine learning decoders can out-perform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but suggest more complex architectures and/or training procedures are necessary to scale to larger code sizes.

.
tldr: This paper applies machine learning to decode circuit-level noise for bivariate bicycle codes, a type of quantum LDPC code.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires efficient decoders; machine learning has shown promise for surface codes but not yet for QLDPC codes.
method: A recurrent, transformer-based neural network is trained to decode circuit-level noise on small bivariate bicycle codes.
result: On a small BB code, the ML decoder achieves lower logical error rates than BP-OSD and consistent runtime, but on a larger code it performs worse while maintaining speed advantage.
conclusion: ML decoders can outperform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but scaling to larger codes requires more complex architectures or training.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes to encode the combinatorial Laplacian, achieving superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide quantum advantages for topological data analysis and related problems.
method: The authors construct a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by operating on a doubled state space of oriented simplices, enabling projection onto harmonic cycles.
result: They demonstrate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedups for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying a QMA-hard problem, and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, without quantum oracles.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes can yield significant speedups for topological data analysis, but the practical relevance depends on the spectral gap and simplex sampling assumptions.

title: Epic-cim: Training Convolutional Neural Networks On A Coherent Ising Machine Via Equilibrium Propagation
authors: Xingrui Yin, Shenwei Kang, Haoqi He, Yan Xiao, Hongdong Zhu, Hai Wei, Yin Ma, Qi Gao, Xiaochun Cao, Kai Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum convolutional neural networks, due to the involvement of quantum measurements and discrete quantum state evolution, face inherent training challenges associated with non-differentiable operations and discrete optimization dynamics, which make conventional gradient-based learning difficult to apply effectively. In this context, energy-based learning provides a promising alternative by reformulating network training as an energy minimization process without explicit gradient backpropagation.In this framework, input data are processed through convolutional operations, followed by quantum sampling to generate intermediate binary representations, while the output layer also relies on quantum sampling to produce final predictions. The overall network energy is composed of convolutional feature matching terms, linear coupling terms at the output layer, and global output constraint terms, enabling both parameter updates and feature evolution to be described through physically interpretable energy dynamics. Furthermore, under the equilibrium propagation mechanism, the energy difference between the free phase and the weakly clamped phase is exploited to drive parameter updates without explicit gradient computation, thereby enabling stable and consistent learning in non-differentiable and discrete spaces. While remaining consistent with classical convolutional learning theory, the proposed framework enhances interpretability and observability through quantum energy modeling, offering a unified physical perspective for efficient QCNN training and the integration of quantum computing with artificial intelligence.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to train convolutional neural networks on a coherent Ising machine using equilibrium propagation, combining classical deep learning with quantum energy-based models.
motivation: Training quantum convolutional neural networks is challenging due to non-differentiable operations and discrete dynamics; energy-based learning offers an alternative without explicit gradient backpropagation.
method: The framework processes input data through convolutional operations and quantum sampling to generate binary representations, then uses equilibrium propagation to update parameters based on energy differences between free and weakly clamped phases.
result: The approach enables stable learning in non-differentiable and discrete spaces while remaining consistent with classical convolutional learning theory.
conclusion: The proposed framework enhances interpretability and observability through quantum energy modeling, offering a unified physical perspective for efficient QCNN training.

title: A Hybrid Classical-Quantum Approach For Multi-Constrained Location Optimization Problem
authors: Jorge Saavedra-Benavides, J. Alejandro Montanez-Barrera, Alberto Maldonado-Romo, Daniel Sierra-Sosa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Maximal Covering Location Problem (MCLP) is an NP-hard Combinatorial Optimization Problem (COP) that aims to determine the optimal facility placements that maximize total coverage. It is characterized by both equality and inequality constraints, which ensure correct coverage but significantly increase the complexity of exploring the solution space as instance size grows. Hybrid quantum-classical approaches might offer a promising alternative to classical optimization methods by enabling the exploration of complex energy landscapes through quantum superposition and probabilistic sampling. In this work, the MCLP is formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model, where constraint embedding plays a critical role in solution quality. In particular, Unbalanced Penalization (UP) is employed as an alternative to the Slack Variables (SV) for handling inequality constraints without increasing the number of variables. This study focuses on QAOA and one of its variants, the WS-QAOA, which leverages a biased initial state derived from a continuous relaxation of the problem. Additionally, a linear ramp (LR) parameter schedule is incorporated to reduce optimization complexity. The performance of these techniques is evaluated both individually and in combination, as a function of circuit depth [MATH] and problem size. Results show that the combined approach of UP, LR, and WS-QAOA consistently improves solution quality and feasibility metrics, while maintaining robust performance as the problem size increases, highlighting its potential within hybrid quantum-classical optimization frameworks.
tldr: This paper applies hybrid quantum-classical optimization (QAOA) to a classical facility location problem, with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.
motivation: The Maximal Covering Location Problem is NP-hard, and classical methods struggle with large instances. Hybrid quantum-classical approaches may offer advantages.
method: The MCLP is formulated as a QUBO problem with inequality constraints handled via Unbalanced Penalization. QAOA and WS-QAOA with a linear ramp schedule are applied and evaluated.
result: The combined approach of UP, LR, and WS-QAOA improves solution quality and feasibility metrics as problem size increases.
conclusion: The hybrid approach shows potential for solving constrained optimization problems, but the work is purely algorithmic and not connected to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Gaussian Reformulation Of The Feynman Path Integral For Quantum Statistical Mechanics With Results For The Second Virial Coefficient Of $^4$He
authors: Phil Attard
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Feynman path integral for quantum statistical mechanics is reformulated as Gaussian sampling of the neighborhood of each position configuration. The variance and mean are obtained from ring polymer statistics on a lattice, and from the high temperature expansion of the Wigner-Kirkwood commutation function, respectively. The algorithm avoids multiple temperature nodes for each configuration and the need for numerical cancelation in the statistical averages, which are problematic for conventional path integral quantum Monte Carlo. Analytic and simulation results for the second virial coefficient of helium are compared to laboratory measurements.
tldr: The paper reformulates the Feynman path integral for quantum statistical mechanics using Gaussian sampling and applies it to compute the second virial coefficient of helium.
motivation: Conventional path integral quantum Monte Carlo methods suffer from numerical cancellation and multiple temperature nodes; a more efficient algorithm is needed.
method: The reformulation uses Gaussian sampling of neighborhood configurations, with variance and mean derived from ring polymer statistics and the high-temperature Wigner-Kirkwood expansion.
result: Analytic and simulation results for the second virial coefficient of helium are compared to laboratory measurements, showing good agreement.
conclusion: The Gaussian reformulation avoids numerical issues of conventional methods and provides accurate results for quantum statistical mechanics.

title: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization Approach For Open-shell Transition-metal Complexes In Gas And Implicit-solvent
authors: David David, Vedangi Pathak, Marek Kowalik, Hamed Mohammadbagherpoor, Vincent Beltrani, Kara Maller, Niall Moroney, Phalgun Lolur
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-shell [MATH] transition-metal complexes challenge electronic-structure methods because competing spin states, charge transfer, and solvation jointly determine their energetics. Here, we combine sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) with the integral-equation-formalism polarizable continuum model (IEF-PCM), extending SQD to correlated open-shell transition-metal systems in a dielectric environment. We investigate the octahedrally coordinated [MATH] complex across two oxidation states, four spin multiplicities, and a metal-ligand dissociation coordinate. We study the Co(III) singlet and quintet states and the Co(II) doublet and quartet states, incorporating open-shell references into SQD-IEF-PCM through an outer self-consistent reaction-field loop. Using samples collected on an IBM Heron quantum processor and active spaces of up to 50 qubits, SQD reproduces coupled-cluster and heat-bath configuration-interaction benchmarks within the same active space in the gas phase and implicit solvent, with a largest observed deviation below 9 [MATH]. Along the dissociation coordinate of high-spin quintet [MATH], SQD resolves an avoided crossing caused by internal charge transfer; this feature is absent in the singlet and the lower oxidation state of the complex. Relative to the gas phase, implicit solvation stabilizes for the quintet state the neutral CO[MATH] dissociation and suppresses the avoided-crossing feature. To our knowledge, this is the first hardware demonstration of SQD for an open-shell [MATH] transition-metal complex in gas phase and implict solvent. These results establish SQD as a robust quantum-centric approach for transition-metal chemistry where spin state ordering, charge transfer, and environmental effects are strongly intertwined.
tldr: This paper applies sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) to open-shell transition-metal complexes in gas and implicit solvent, demonstrating a quantum-centric approach for correlated electronic structure calculations.
motivation: Accurate modeling of open-shell transition-metal complexes is challenging due to competing spin states, charge transfer, and solvation effects; classical methods are computationally expensive.
method: The authors combine SQD with the integral-equation-formalism polarizable continuum model (IEF-PCM) and use an outer self-consistent reaction-field loop to incorporate open-shell references. Samples are collected on an IBM Heron quantum processor with active spaces up to 50 qubits.
result: SQD reproduces coupled-cluster and heat-bath configuration-interaction benchmarks within the same active space, with deviations below 9 mHa. It resolves an avoided crossing in the high-spin quintet state along a dissociation coordinate, which is suppressed by implicit solvation.
conclusion: SQD is established as a robust quantum-centric approach for transition-metal chemistry where spin state ordering, charge transfer, and environmental effects are intertwined.

title: Remote Infrared Absorption Spectroscopy With Undetected Photons
authors: Simon Neves, F\'eriel Armbruster, Jean-Pierre Wolf
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a novel method for remote open-path Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy with undetected photons. Similar to previous quantum spectroscopy works, a mid-infrared spectrum is reconstructed by detecting a near-infrared radiation only, thus bypassing important limitations of infrared detectors. Our study however relies on the co-propagation of the photon-pair and the pump-laser over the same optical path, which allows the probing of the open atmosphere over long distances. By sending the photons over unprecedented distances of up-to 43.4m in the outdoor atmosphere, we were able to detect butane released in the open-path, as well as natural atmospheric methane, thus demonstrating the first use of infrared spectroscopy with undetected photons for atmospheric measurements.
tldr: This paper demonstrates remote open-path Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy using undetected photons for atmospheric gas detection.
motivation: Infrared detectors have limitations; using undetected photons allows mid-infrared spectroscopy with near-infrared detection, enabling long-distance atmospheric measurements.
method: The authors use a nonlinear interferometer where mid-infrared photons are generated but not detected; instead, correlated near-infrared photons are measured to reconstruct the absorption spectrum. The pump laser and photon pairs co-propagate over the same open path up to 43.4 m.
result: Butane and natural atmospheric methane were detected over outdoor distances up to 43.4 m, demonstrating the first use of this technique for atmospheric measurements.
conclusion: This method enables remote infrared absorption spectroscopy without requiring sensitive mid-infrared detectors, with potential applications in environmental monitoring and security.

title: Measuring The Dipole Phase Of Bloch-trajectory Harmonics Using A Monolithic Interferometer
authors: Mohanad Awad, Julian Sp\"athe, Paramjit C. Yadav, Mandakini Bhat, Zsolt Div\'eki, Eric Cormier, B\'alint Kiss, Eszter Barad\'acs, J\'anos Tom\'an, Zolt\'an Erd\'elyi, Thomas Siefke, Adrian N. Pfeiffer, Matthias K\"ubel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncovering the dipole phase of gas-phase high harmonic generation was instrumental to understanding the recollision physics underlying attosecond pulse generation. Corresponding measurements in the condensed phase have not yet yielded a consistent picture. Here, we present a compact and inherently stable approach to high-harmonic interferometry in thin-film solids. We employ it to reveal the dipole phase of high-harmonic generation in polycrystalline ZnO, driven by broadband mid-IR laser pulses. We demonstrate that, under the conditions of our experiments, recollisions facilitated by Bloch oscillations represent the dominant contribution to high-harmonic generation just above the bandgap.
tldr: This paper presents a compact interferometer to measure the dipole phase of high-harmonic generation in solids, focusing on Bloch oscillations in ZnO.
motivation: Understanding the dipole phase in condensed-phase high-harmonic generation is important for attosecond science, but previous measurements have been inconsistent.
method: A monolithic interferometer is used to perform high-harmonic interferometry in thin-film polycrystalline ZnO driven by mid-IR laser pulses.
result: The dipole phase is measured, showing that recollisions facilitated by Bloch oscillations dominate high-harmonic generation just above the bandgap.
conclusion: The work provides a stable method for measuring dipole phases in solids, advancing attosecond metrology in condensed matter.

title: Representation-Dependent Machine Learning Of The Isotropic-Nematic Transition In The Lebwohl-Lasher Model
authors: Maninder Kaur, Aojie Xue, David P Landau
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning detection of phase transitions depends not only on the learning algorithm, but also on whether the input representation preserves the symmetries of the system. We examine this for the weak first-order isotropic--nematic transition of the three-dimensional Lebwohl--Lasher model, whose apolar and continuously degenerate nematic phase makes raw molecular configurations a challenging input for unsupervised learning.
