title: Cubic-in-magnetization Contributions To The Magneto-optic Kerr Effect Investigated For Ni(001) And Ni(111) Thin Films
authors: Robin Silber, Maik Gaerner, Kamil Postava, Jaroslav Hamrle, And Timo Kuschel
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Silber, Maik Gaerner, Kamil Postava, Jaroslav Hamrle, and Timo Kuschel

The existence of higher-order effects in magnetization in magneto-transport and magneto-optic phenomena is well known. These effects are of importance not only in research but also directly in applications. Anisotropic magneto-resistance, anisotropic magneto-thermopower, quadratic magneto-optic Kerr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014418] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates higher-order magneto-optic Kerr effects in nickel thin films, focusing on cubic-in-magnetization contributions.
motivation: Higher-order magneto-optic effects are important for both fundamental research and applications, but their detailed characterization in nickel films is lacking.
method: The authors measure the magneto-optic Kerr effect for Ni(001) and Ni(111) thin films and analyze the cubic-in-magnetization contributions using symmetry arguments and experimental data.
result: They identify and quantify the cubic-in-magnetization contributions to the Kerr effect, showing distinct behaviors for different crystallographic orientations.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed understanding of higher-order magneto-optic effects in nickel, which may be relevant for magnetic sensing and spintronics applications.

title: Origin Of Acceptor Preference In Silicon, Diamond, And Silicon Carbide
authors: Xuefen Cai, Feiyang Chen, Huachun Wang, Yi-Feng Zheng, Bin Wang, And Su-Huai Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Xuefen Cai, Feiyang Chen, Huachun Wang, Yi-Feng Zheng, Bin Wang, and Su-Huai Wei

Silicon, diamond, and their compound silicon carbide play pivotal roles in electronic science and technology. Trivalent impurities such as B and Al are the typical choices for [MATH]-type doping in these semiconductors. Intriguingly, B dominates in Si and diamond, while Al is preferred in SiC for indus…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045203] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the origin of acceptor preference (B vs Al) in silicon, diamond, and silicon carbide semiconductors using first-principles calculations.
motivation: Understanding why B is preferred in Si and diamond while Al is preferred in SiC is important for optimizing p-type doping in these technologically crucial semiconductors.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) are performed to analyze the electronic structure and formation energies of B and Al acceptors in Si, diamond, and SiC.
result: The preference is explained by differences in atomic size, electronegativity, and the resulting lattice relaxation and electronic effects.
conclusion: The study provides a unified explanation for acceptor preference across these materials, aiding in the design of better p-type dopants.

title: Computer Simulations Of The Stark Effect In The Helium-$β$ Complex Of Krypton In Inertial Confinement Fusion Conditions
authors: G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, And M. A. Gigosos
abstract:
Author(s): G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, and M. A. Gigosos

There is an ongoing interest in using spectroscopy in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments, where dopants such as krypton can provide vital information about the temperature and density of the imploding plasma. While the most advanced tools for calculating Stark profiles are computer simula…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015212] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses computer simulations to study the Stark effect in krypton under inertial confinement fusion conditions, focusing on plasma spectroscopy.
motivation: To improve diagnostic capabilities in inertial confinement fusion experiments by modeling spectral line shapes of dopant krypton.
method: Computer simulations of Stark-broadened line profiles for the helium-beta complex of krypton in dense plasmas.
result: Simulated Stark profiles that can be used to infer plasma temperature and density from spectroscopic data.
conclusion: The simulations provide a tool for interpreting ICF spectra, but the work is applied plasma physics with no quantum information or thermodynamics contribution.

title: Dynamical Origin Of Extreme Events In Mutually Coupled And Networked Brusselator
authors: S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, And I. Manimehan
abstract:
Author(s): S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, and I. Manimehan

This study investigates the dynamical origins and statistical properties of extreme events (EEs) in a diffusively coupled theoretical Brusselator system, extending from pairwise interactions to globally coupled networks. Statistically, the emergence of EEs is characterized by heavy-tailed probabilit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014217] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies extreme events in a diffusively coupled Brusselator system, a chemical reaction model, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamical origin of extreme events in nonlinear systems is important for predicting rare but impactful phenomena.
method: The authors analyze a diffusively coupled Brusselator model, from pairwise to globally coupled networks, using statistical and dynamical systems methods.
result: Extreme events are characterized by heavy-tailed probability distributions and are linked to specific dynamical instabilities.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the emergence of extreme events in coupled nonlinear oscillators, but does not involve quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Unified Ott-Antonsen Framework For Stability And Bifurcations In Ring Swarmalators
authors: Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, And Xingang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, and Xingang Wang

Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014212] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for analyzing stability and bifurcations in ring swarmalator systems, which combine phase oscillations with spatial swarming.
motivation: Swarmalators exhibit rich collective dynamics, but a general theoretical framework for their stability and bifurcations was lacking.
method: The authors extend the Ott-Antonsen ansatz to ring swarmalator models, deriving reduced equations for the order parameters and analyzing their stability and bifurcations.
result: They obtain analytical conditions for synchronization, clustering, and wave states, and validate them with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a powerful tool for understanding collective behavior in active matter systems with both phase and spatial degrees of freedom.

title: Filtered Rayleigh-Ritz And The Prony-Ritz Equivalence Class
authors: Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, And Michael L. Wagman
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, and Michael L. Wagman

Recent work [ 112, 054506 (2025);
tldr: This paper presents a method for extracting energy spectra from correlation functions in lattice quantum field theory using a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz approach and establishes an equivalence class with Prony-type methods.
motivation: Extracting excited-state energies and matrix elements from Euclidean correlation functions is a fundamental challenge in lattice QCD, and existing methods like the Lanczos algorithm have limitations.
method: The authors develop a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz method that uses a filtering function to isolate eigenstates, and show that it is equivalent to a class of Prony-like methods, providing a unified framework.
result: The method yields accurate energy levels and matrix elements for test systems, and the equivalence class clarifies the relationship between different extraction techniques.
conclusion: The filtered Rayleigh-Ritz approach offers a robust and systematic way to extract spectral information from correlation functions, with connections to other methods that enhance its utility.

title: Inhibition Of Explosive Transitions In Spreading Dynamics By Nonlinear Higher-order Adaptation
authors: Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, And Shaoting Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, and Shaoting Tang

The coevolution of structure and dynamics, known as adaptation, is a fundamental property in various systems and drives diverse emergent behaviors. However, the adaptation in most works primarily stems from pairwise situations, which is insufficient to capture ubiquitous higher-order characteristics…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033068] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how nonlinear higher-order adaptation can inhibit explosive transitions in spreading dynamics on complex networks.
motivation: Explosive transitions in spreading dynamics are undesirable in many real systems, and understanding how adaptation mechanisms can prevent them is important for controlling epidemics or information spread.
method: The authors develop a model of spreading dynamics with higher-order (non-pairwise) adaptation rules and analyze it using mean-field theory and numerical simulations on synthetic and real networks.
result: They find that nonlinear higher-order adaptation can effectively suppress explosive transitions, leading to continuous phase transitions instead.
conclusion: Higher-order adaptation mechanisms provide a robust way to control explosive spreading phenomena, offering insights for designing resilient networks.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy, using time-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in van der Waals heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling the microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) to probe the dynamics of charge transfer in a heterostructure under different excitation energies.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways for charge transfer that depend on the excitation energy, revealing a competition between direct and indirect transfer mechanisms.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into how excitation energy can be used to control charge transfer pathways, which may help optimize device performance.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism underlying abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical framework for abrupt learning in recurrent networks, with implications for training dynamics.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in two-dimensional photonic crystals with stealthy hyperuniform disorder, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of radiative loss in disordered photonic materials, impacting their design for optical applications.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper aims to review three real-space techniques that provide direct access to such information.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can reveal atomic-scale details of disorder in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes offers a more comprehensive understanding of atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.

title: Physical Sampling For Computational Photography
authors: Ni Chen And David J Brady
abstract: The standard model of photography is that lenses form images and focal planes capture those images. Over the past two decades, however, cameras have been transformed from devices that record focal images into analog-to-digital converters that transform massively parallel optical signals into serial electronic data. Under this new model, one may choose to maximize the quality and quantity of captured information, rather than focal image quality. Here we review the nature of the optical data stream and consider lens and focal plane designs that improve information capture capacity. After maximizing information capacity, the challenge of converting this information to digital data requires novel read-out and compression. We review strategies for approaching physical information limits under realistic size, power, and bandwidth constraints. Multiscale monocentric (spherical primary optics combined with arrays of secondary micro-cameras, each imaging a narrow subfield) and array lens architectures relax unfavorable geometric scaling by trading monolithic optics for co-designed system-level integration (jointly optimized optics, focal-plane, and readout subsystems). Metaoptic and mode-sorting focal plane filters implement richer projection operators that sample spectral, polarimetric, and coherence features without requiring exhaustive scanning. Finally, because readout and computation dominate energy at high throughput, we highlight architectures that perform dimensionality reduction before (or during) digitization, including integrated photonic encoders and multilayer optical projections coupled to detection and learned decoding. Together, these developments motivate a shift from cameras optimized to produce 2D images toward cameras engineered as end-to-end information channels, co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout to deliver more task-relevant measurements per photon and per joule.
tldr: This paper reviews computational photography architectures that optimize information capture and readout under physical constraints, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to shift camera design from producing 2D images to engineering end-to-end information channels, maximizing task-relevant measurements per photon and per joule.
method: The paper reviews multiscale monocentric optics, metaoptic filters, and integrated photonic encoders that perform dimensionality reduction before digitization.
result: It identifies architectures that improve information capture capacity and energy efficiency by co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout subsystems.
conclusion: Future cameras should be designed as information channels rather than image recorders, leveraging co-design to overcome scaling and power constraints.

title: Dynamic Mean-variance Portfolio Selection With No-shorting Constraints And Unknown Investment Opportunity Sets
authors: Xun Li, Yutian Wang, Xun Yu Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection with no-shorting constraints and unknown investment opportunity sets from a reinforcement learning (RL) perspective. The problem is a constrained stochastic linear -- quadratic control problem for which the entropy-regularized exploratory formulation of Wang et al. (2020) leads to difficulty in theoretical analysis, because enforcing the constraint on the support of randomized policies nullifies the tractable Gaussian exploration. To tackle this challenge, we introduce an auxiliary exploratory problem without entropy in which exploratory policies are still Gaussian whose samples may violate the no-shorting requirement but their means satisfy it. We then prove that, for a suitable choice of exploration variance, the mean of the optimal Gaussian policy of the auxiliary problem coincides with the optimal policy of the original problem. Motivated by this theoretical result, we develop a model-free RL algorithm that learns the optimal policy of the auxiliary (and hence the original) problem directly from trajectory data without estimating the investment opportunity set. A numerical example demonstrates the performance of the proposed algorithm.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection with no-shorting constraints and unknown investment opportunity sets using reinforcement learning.
motivation: The problem is a constrained stochastic linear-quadratic control problem where standard entropy-regularized exploration fails due to constraints on the support of randomized policies.
method: An auxiliary exploratory problem without entropy is introduced, where Gaussian policies are used but their means satisfy the no-shorting constraint; a model-free RL algorithm learns the optimal policy from trajectory data.
result: For a suitable exploration variance, the mean of the optimal Gaussian policy of the auxiliary problem coincides with the optimal policy of the original problem.
conclusion: The proposed RL algorithm effectively solves the constrained portfolio selection problem without estimating the investment opportunity set.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for applications in micro- and nano-electromechanical systems.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and classical molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer binding and sliding friction in hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN).
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate the interlayer binding energy and friction force, enabling reversible switching between low-friction and high-friction states.
conclusion: Electric fields provide a viable route for active control of friction in layered materials, with potential applications in nanoscale devices.

title: Relativistic Bound-state Solutions For A Non-central Schi{\"o}berg-type Hyperbolic Potential With Double Ring-shaped Angular Terms
authors: Vatan H. Badalov Shakir. M. Nagiyev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Singular interactions can reshape quantum spectra by changing admissible wavefunction domains. In this study, we investigate this mechanism in the Klein--Gordon equation for a non-central Schi\"oberg-type hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular barriers. Equal scalar and vector couplings separate the radial and angular dynamics. We solve the angular equation exactly and treat the radial equation with the Greene--Aldrich approximation, obtaining Jacobi-polynomial wavefunctions and an implicit relativistic quantization condition. The equatorial inverse-square singularity splits configuration space into reflection-related sectors with identical angular spectra. Reducing the barrier to zero within one sector retains only odd-parity states, unlike the regular full-domain problem, which restores both parities. The nonrelativistic limit recovers the Schr{\"o}dinger spectrum. For NaH and Na[MATH], low-lying vibrational energies agree reasonably with experiment, whereas near-dissociation deviations reveal asymptotic limitations.
tldr: This paper solves the Klein-Gordon equation for a non-central hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular terms, obtaining bound-state solutions and comparing with experimental data for diatomic molecules.
motivation: To understand how singular interactions modify quantum spectra in relativistic settings, particularly for non-central potentials with angular barriers.
method: Separation of variables with equal scalar and vector couplings, exact angular solution, and Greene-Aldrich approximation for the radial equation, yielding Jacobi-polynomial wavefunctions.
result: Implicit relativistic quantization condition; angular spectrum identical in reflection-related sectors; zero-barrier limit retains only odd-parity states; nonrelativistic limit recovers Schrödinger spectrum.
conclusion: The model shows reasonable agreement with experimental vibrational energies for NaH and Na2 at low levels, but deviations near dissociation indicate asymptotic limitations.

title: Frame Representation Of The First-Order Part Of The Laplace-Beltrami Operator
authors: A. G. Nuramatov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the geometric content of the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator on an oriented Riemannian manifold. Relative to an arbitrary local orthonormal frame, the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator defines a distinguished vector field, whose coefficients are expressed through the Levi--Civita connection forms. The corresponding one-form determines a covariant derivative whose connection factorization removes the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator and replaces it by a natural scalar potential. The construction is frame dependent. We show that its transformation under local rotations of the orthonormal frame compensates the corresponding variation of the sum-of-squares part, leaving the full Laplace--Beltrami operator invariant. These results reveal the geometric role of the first-order part of the Laplace--Beltrami operator.
tldr: This paper studies the geometric content of the first-order part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on Riemannian manifolds, focusing on frame-dependent constructions.
motivation: To understand the geometric role of the first-order part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator and its transformation under local rotations of orthonormal frames.
method: The authors analyze the first-order part relative to an arbitrary local orthonormal frame, expressing coefficients via Levi-Civita connection forms, and study its transformation properties.
result: The first-order part defines a distinguished vector field and a one-form that determines a covariant derivative, whose connection factorization removes the first-order part and replaces it with a scalar potential.
conclusion: The construction reveals the geometric role of the first-order part and shows that its transformation compensates the variation of the sum-of-squares part, leaving the full operator invariant.

title: Nonuniform And Inequitable Healthcare Accessibility Losses During Flooding-amplified Congestion Across Us Cities
authors: Raviraj Dave, Danish Mansoor Tantary, Dongqin Zhou, Udit Bhatia, Auroop R. Ganguly
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cities in the United States and worldwide concentrate populations with diverse incomes, demographics and health risks, making access to healthcare facilities and emergency services critical. Urban flooding amplifies congestion and further degrades healthcare accessibility, but its impacts are uneven within and across cities, often burdening underserved populations and underplanned areas. These risks are intensifying as rapid development, aging infrastructure and climate change increase urban flood exposure. Across 30 of the most populous US cities, we show that peak-hour congestion alone reduces accessibility by 4% to 29%, while flooding further reduces it by 2% to more than 90%. These losses depend on flood type, transportation design, infrastructure planning, health vulnerability and spatial inequality. Flooding also increases spatial inequality in healthcare access, but the social burden varies by city and flood type, with urban coastal flooding disproportionately affecting less socially vulnerable populations in the United States. Our findings suggest that targeted approaches for embedding flood resilience in transportation and healthcare systems will be more effective than universal strategies, while allowing cities to learn from diverse urban regions facing similar accessibility risks.
tldr: This paper studies how flooding amplifies congestion and reduces healthcare accessibility across US cities, highlighting spatial inequality.
motivation: Urban flooding exacerbates healthcare access disparities, but its uneven impacts across cities and populations are poorly understood.
method: The authors analyze 30 US cities using traffic and flood models to quantify accessibility losses under peak-hour congestion and various flood scenarios.
result: Peak-hour congestion reduces accessibility by 4-29%, and flooding further reduces it by 2% to over 90%, with coastal flooding disproportionately affecting less socially vulnerable populations.
conclusion: Targeted resilience strategies are more effective than universal approaches, and cities can learn from each other's experiences.

title: Smoothed Two-Stage Decomposition Algorithm For Solving Large-Scale Transmission And Distribution Ac-opf Problems
authors: Juan Ospina, Manuel Garcia, Xinyi Luo, Andreas Wachter, David M. Fobes, Russell Bent
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) into the power grid has introduced new challenges to AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) problems. Traditional OPF optimize consider transmission systems, treating distribution networks as static loads. However, the growing presence of DERs makes accurate distribution system modeling crucial for grid operations. Consequently, efficiently solving the resultant large-scale, nonconvex transmission and distribution (T&D) AC-OPF problem remains a significant challenge. This paper proposes a Smoothed Two-Stage Decomposition Optimizer (StsDOpt) to address these complexities by decomposing the T&D AC-OPF problem into a master-subproblem(s) structure, enabling parallel solving. Unlike traditional methods, StsDOpt does not rely on approximations or relaxations. It uses a smoothing technique to render the subproblems responses differentiable with respect to the master problem, leveraging the barrier problem properties inherent in primal-dual interior point methods. This approach is crucial for accurately modeling and solving distribution systems, which are multiphase, unbalanced, and nonlinear, distinguishing StsDOpt apart from other methods. Integrated into the PowerModelsITD framework, StsDOpt has been validated through numerical experiments, demonstrating reduced wall-clock solve time and increased scalability. Results highlight its efficacy as a robust, scalable solution for large-scale T&D AC-OPF problems, facilitating the reliable integration of DERs into complex T&D systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a smoothed two-stage decomposition algorithm for solving large-scale transmission and distribution AC optimal power flow problems.
motivation: The integration of distributed energy resources introduces challenges to AC-OPF, requiring accurate distribution system modeling.
method: The algorithm decomposes the problem into a master-subproblem structure, using smoothing to make subproblem responses differentiable, and solves in parallel.
result: Numerical experiments show reduced wall-clock solve time and increased scalability compared to traditional methods.
conclusion: The proposed method is a robust, scalable solution for large-scale T&D AC-OPF problems, facilitating DER integration.

title: Surrogate-to-code Verification Of A Non-intrusive Pod-gpr Machine-learning Emulator Of Peak Thermomechanical Fields, With Application To A Carbon-carbon Aircraft Brake Disc
authors: Franklin Kamche
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While non-intrusive reduced-order emulators successfully substitute for costly finite-element simulations, certification-grade applications demand a rigorous error assessment relative to the solver's own discretization uncertainty. This work introduces a verification framework designed to evaluate prediction accuracy directly against this numerical uncertainty floor, rather than physical observation. We demonstrate this approach on a carbon-carbon aircraft brake disc during a rejected take-off scenario, predicting peak temperature and peak von Mises stress fields. Operating over a fixed mesh of 60914 nodes, the emulator relies on a pipeline coupling proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and Gaussian process regression (GPR) parameterized by 5 inputs. We formulate an algebraically exact, a posteriori error budget that isolates the emulator's signed error into distinct truncation and regression components at the extremum. This error is then evaluated against a discretization floor established via mesh-convergence studies on the peak quantities of interest. On a completely independent test set, our emulator matches the high-fidelity solver's peak values within its own discretization uncertainty for both fields, a benchmark we define as surrogate-to-code fidelity. Notably, the residual error stems primarily from linear reduction limits rather than regression inaccuracies. Beyond the main framework, we present two secondary contributions: the concurrent, non-intrusive prediction of the thermal and mechanical peaks, and a probabilistic approach to spatial zone localization for these extrema. This methodology applies to non-intrusive reduced-order models of parameterized finite-element simulations wherever a discretization-error estimate for the quantity of interest can be obtained.
tldr: This paper presents a verification framework for a POD-GPR emulator of peak thermomechanical fields in a carbon-carbon aircraft brake disc, comparing predictions to the solver's discretization uncertainty.
motivation: Certification-grade applications require rigorous error assessment of reduced-order emulators relative to numerical uncertainty, not physical observation.
method: The emulator uses proper orthogonal decomposition and Gaussian process regression on a fixed mesh; an a posteriori error budget isolates truncation and regression components, evaluated against a discretization floor from mesh-convergence studies.
result: The emulator matches the high-fidelity solver's peak values within its discretization uncertainty; residual error stems primarily from linear reduction limits.
conclusion: The methodology applies to non-intrusive reduced-order models of parameterized finite-element simulations where discretization-error estimates are available.

title: History-Dependent Recursive Preferences In Markov Decision Processes
authors: William B. Haskell
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In finite horizon dynamic programming with history-dependent preferences, the relevant state may be the entire realized history, even when the physical state is Markov. This paper develops a behavioral state-reduction theory for such Markov decision processes. Under behavioral axioms and a certainty-equivalent richness condition, the full-history problem admits a recursive representation composed of time and risk aggregators. We then derive a canonical preference-augmented (PA) state by quotienting histories that have the same current physical Markov state, are indifferent under every common continuation plan, and remain equivalent after every common one-step extension. This canonical PA state is minimal among reachable recursive factorizations of the underlying preferences. Under Markov feasibility and standard dynamic-programming regularity, a PA Bellman selector induces an optimal full-history policy. With additional rectangularity and exhaustiveness conditions, we reparameterize the preference memory into distinct belief and taste coordinates, and obtain a separated representation and Bellman recursion. We give a taxonomy of examples to illustrate the scope of our framework.
tldr: This paper develops a behavioral state-reduction theory for Markov decision processes with history-dependent preferences, deriving a canonical preference-augmented state and recursive representation.
motivation: In finite horizon dynamic programming, history-dependent preferences make the state space explode even when the physical state is Markov, so a state-reduction method is needed.
method: The paper uses behavioral axioms and a certainty-equivalent richness condition to derive a recursive representation with time and risk aggregators, then constructs a canonical preference-augmented state by quotienting histories.
result: A minimal canonical PA state is obtained, and under additional conditions a separated representation with belief and taste coordinates is derived, leading to a Bellman recursion.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled way to reduce the state space in dynamic programming with history-dependent preferences, with potential applications in economics and decision theory.

title: On High Probability Of Universal Approximation In Random Basis Expansions With Non-continuous Weight Sampling
authors: John E. Darges
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random basis expansion (RBE) search the span of a randomly sampled basis to find the best approximation of a target function. They are equivalent to single layer neural networks where the hidden layer weights are chosen randomly. Universal approximation properties have been established for RBEs using continuous weight sampling distributions and real-valued activation functions. Our results extend the universal approximation property to RBEs that use non-continuous weight distributions with dense support in the weight space and that use complex-valued activation functions. The result shows such random bases have the universal approximation property with arbitrarily high probability.
tldr: This paper proves universal approximation properties for random basis expansions with non-continuous weight sampling and complex-valued activation functions.
motivation: Extend universal approximation results to more general weight distributions and activation functions, which are relevant for neural network theory.
method: The authors analyze random basis expansions with non-continuous weight distributions having dense support and complex-valued activation functions, proving that such bases can approximate any target function with high probability.
result: They show that random bases with non-continuous weight distributions and complex-valued activations have the universal approximation property with arbitrarily high probability.
conclusion: The results broaden the theoretical foundation of random basis expansions and single-layer neural networks.

title: Identifiability Of Partial-Mastery Cognitive Diagnostic Models
authors: Jun Wu, Patr\'icia Martinkov\'a, Elena Erosheva
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial-mastery (PM) cognitive diagnostic models (CDMs) extend traditional CDMs by replacing binary latent attribute mastery indicators with continuous mastery scores for multiple latent attributes. In PM-CDMs, each subject is characterized by a fixed continuous latent mastery vector, from which item-specific binary attribute profiles are independently generated. This formulation provides a bridge between classical CDMs and continuous latent variable models. Despite growing interest in PM-CDMs, their identifiability properties remain unexplored. In this work, we establish the first identifiability results for PM-CDMs. We derive sufficient conditions for identifiability that are direct analogues of established conditions for traditional CDMs. To develop the main argument, we use symbolic computation on a minimal example with five items and two latent attributes to show that the Jacobian of the model parameterization is generically nonzero. Combining tools from real analysis and algebraic statistics, we prove that this local property implies generic finite-to-one identifiability of the item parameters and the marginal distributions of the relevant latent attributes. We further show that if the [MATH]-matrix contains such identifiable local structures for all attribute pairs, identifiability extends to the full PM-CDM. These findings provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for estimation and inference in partial-mastery cognitive diagnostic models.
tldr: This paper establishes identifiability conditions for partial-mastery cognitive diagnostic models, which are statistical models for educational measurement.
motivation: Partial-mastery cognitive diagnostic models extend traditional CDMs by using continuous latent attributes, but their identifiability properties were unknown, hindering reliable estimation and inference.
method: The authors derive sufficient conditions for identifiability analogous to those for traditional CDMs, using symbolic computation on a minimal example and combining real analysis with algebraic statistics to prove generic finite-to-one identifiability.
result: They show that if the Q-matrix contains identifiable local structures for all attribute pairs, identifiability extends to the full PM-CDM, providing the first identifiability results for these models.
conclusion: These findings provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for estimation and inference in partial-mastery cognitive diagnostic models.

title: Quantum Sugawara Operators In $\mathrm{U}_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_{M|N})$
authors: Naihuan Jing, Ming Liu, Jian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct Sugawara operators for the quantum affine superalgebra [MATH] in an explicit form which generalizes the results given in for the quantum affine algebras. We also calculate the Harish-Chandra images of the Sugawara operators.
tldr: This paper constructs Sugawara operators for the quantum affine superalgebra U_q(gl_{M|N}), generalizing previous results for quantum affine algebras.
motivation: Sugawara operators are important in representation theory and conformal field theory; extending them to superalgebras is a natural mathematical generalization.
method: The authors provide an explicit construction of Sugawara operators for the quantum affine superalgebra and compute their Harish-Chandra images.
result: Explicit formulas for Sugawara operators in the quantum affine superalgebra setting are obtained.
conclusion: The work extends known results to superalgebras, contributing to the representation theory of quantum groups.

title: Sustainable Air-Ground Integrated Coverage Networks: Iscc Architecture, Technologies, And Testbed
authors: J. Liu, X. Zhang, M. Sheng, R. Zhang, N. Zhao, J. Wang, J. Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid emergence of sixth-generation (6G) networks and the low-altitude economy has accelerated the evolution of wireless infrastructures toward air-ground integrated coverage networks (AGICNs), which seamlessly fuse terrestrial and aerial communication resources. However, existing AGICN studies primarily focus on coverage enhancement, while ignoring sustainability. Pursuing sustainable AGICNs introduces new challenges due to the multidimensional resource coupling across heterogeneous air-ground segments. In view of this, this paper presents a comprehensive survey and tutorial on sustainable AGICNs, aiming to balance coverage capacity with carbon efficiency in low-altitude economies. An integrated sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC)-driven architecture, which enables dynamic resource orchestration through closed-loop control, is proposed. We thus introduce a multi-dimensional sustainability metric system, which covers operational efficiency, task-oriented performance, and full lifecycle carbon emissions, to quantify energy and carbon footprints. We review enabling technologies, including artificial intelligence, hybrid precoding, integrated sensing and communication, and simultaneous wireless information and power transfer, and discuss their integration into the ISCC framework to minimize energy consumption while maintaining robust coverage. Experimental results on a real-world testbed demonstrate a 20% reduction in power consumption while achieving over 90% coverage probability, highlighting the feasibility of sustainable AGICNs for future green networks.
tldr: This paper surveys sustainable air-ground integrated coverage networks using an ISCC architecture, focusing on coverage and carbon efficiency.
motivation: Existing air-ground integrated networks focus on coverage but ignore sustainability; this work aims to balance coverage with carbon efficiency.
method: The paper proposes an ISCC-driven architecture with closed-loop resource orchestration, reviews enabling technologies like AI and hybrid precoding, and validates on a testbed.
result: Experimental results show 20% reduction in power consumption while achieving over 90% coverage probability.
conclusion: The proposed sustainable AGICN framework demonstrates feasibility for future green networks.

title: Topological Weak Mixing For Certain Linear Involutions Of Hyperelliptic Type
authors: Felipe Arbul\'u, Basti\'an Espinoza, Alejandro Maass
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A linear involution is an injective piecewise isometry defined on a pair of disjoint intervals. They are defined by a combinatorial data given by a generalized permutation and a length vector. As it was done for interval exchange transformations, it is conjectured that, except for some combinatorial data, a typical linear involution is measure-theoretically weakly mixing. In this direction, one may first explore the question of topological weak mixing for topological models of linear involutions. In this article we prove topological weak mixing for the natural symbolic codings of typical linear involutions defined by some generalized permutations of hyperelliptic type. We consider the generalized permutation \[ \sigma_{s,r} = 0 & A & 1 & 2 & \cdots & s & A & s+1 & s+2 & \cdots & s+r \\ s+r & \cdots & s+2 & s+1 & B & s & \cdots & 2 & 1 & B & 0 . \] We prove that the natural symbolic coding of a typical linear involution defined by a generalized permutation in the Rauzy class of [MATH] is topologically weakly mixing, provided that it has at least a simple letter and its associated genus is sufficiently large.
tldr: This paper proves topological weak mixing for symbolic codings of certain linear involutions of hyperelliptic type, a result in dynamical systems.
motivation: The paper aims to understand weak mixing properties of linear involutions, which are piecewise isometries on intervals, as a step towards proving measure-theoretic weak mixing for typical linear involutions.
method: The authors consider a specific family of generalized permutations of hyperelliptic type and analyze the natural symbolic coding of the associated linear involutions, using combinatorial and topological arguments.
result: They prove that for typical linear involutions in the Rauzy class of these permutations, the symbolic coding is topologically weakly mixing, provided the permutation has at least one simple letter and sufficiently large genus.
conclusion: This result contributes to the ergodic theory of linear involutions, extending known results for interval exchange transformations to this related class of dynamical systems.

title: On The Spectral Synthesis Of Lipschitz Persistence Diagram Vectorizations
authors: Mehmet Emin Aktas Charles Fanning
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A persistence diagram represents the birth and death of homology classes along a filtration as a multiset of intervals, and we consider persistence diagram vectorizations to be maps [MATH] sending persistence diagrams over a metric pair [MATH] to values in a Banach space [MATH]. We prove an isometric isomorphism between Lipschitz extensions of vectorizations, modulo constants, on the Grothendieck completion [MATH] of [MATH] and the bounded [MATH]-cocycles for the translation action of [MATH] on [MATH]. We then prove that if every bounded linear functional on [MATH] maps a Lipschitz extension of a vectorization to the sum of an additive homomorphism from [MATH] to [MATH] and a Fourier--Stieltjes transform of a finite complex regular Borel measure on [MATH], then the associated cocycle generates a synthesizable variety. We extend spectral synthesis to Lipschitz vectorizations of persistence diagrams on separable metric pairs and show whether examples of persistence diagram vectorizations in the literature have Lipschitz extensions with spectral synthesis.
tldr: This paper studies spectral synthesis for Lipschitz vectorizations of persistence diagrams, a topic in topological data analysis.
motivation: To understand the functional analytic properties of persistence diagram vectorizations, specifically whether Lipschitz extensions admit spectral synthesis.
method: The authors prove an isometric isomorphism between Lipschitz extensions of vectorizations and bounded cocycles, and then extend spectral synthesis to Lipschitz vectorizations on separable metric pairs.
result: They show that under certain conditions, the associated cocycle generates a synthesizable variety, and they examine existing vectorizations for spectral synthesis.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for spectral synthesis of persistence diagram vectorizations, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Composable Verification Pipelines For Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Andreas Br\"annstr\"om Julian Alfredo Mendez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing approaches for reasoning about action and change provide expressive semantics for modeling dynamic systems, in most cases built on top of logic programming systems. We introduce a modular framework for transition and trajectory verification based on Tiles and implemented in Soda, which is an efficient functional programming language. The framework operationalizes action language semantics through executable verification pipelines that process states, actions, transitions, and rules as compositional functional components. Verification procedures are represented as typed functional pipelines, enabling modular specifications, reusable reasoning components, and transparent execution workflows with guaranteed pipeline termination. The framework includes an executable specification layer that allows users to define domain descriptions in YAML, which are operationalized into the underlying verification model and executable pipeline structure. We provide an open-source implementation and illustrate the framework through examples that involve misinformation and emotional reasoning.
tldr: A modular framework for transition and trajectory verification in multi-agent systems using functional programming pipelines.
motivation: Existing approaches for reasoning about action and change lack modularity and composability, making verification of dynamic systems cumbersome.
method: Introduces Tiles, a framework implemented in Soda, that operationalizes action language semantics as typed functional pipelines processing states, actions, transitions, and rules.
result: Provides executable verification pipelines with guaranteed termination, and an executable specification layer using YAML for domain descriptions.
conclusion: The framework enables modular, reusable, and transparent verification of multi-agent systems, demonstrated with examples involving misinformation and emotional reasoning.

title: Boundary-Seeking GAN-Augmented TabTransformer For Adversarially Robust Intrusion Detection
authors: Aliyah Kurniasih Raihan Sultan Pasha Basuki
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) often suffer from class imbalance and vulnerability to adversarial attacks, leading to degraded detection performance and reduced robustness. This study proposes a TabTransformer framework augmented by the Boundary-Seeking Generative Adversarial Network (BGAN) for flow-based intrusion detection using the CICIDS2017 dataset. BGAN serves a dual purpose by generating synthetic minority-class samples to mitigate data imbalance and producing adversarial samples to evaluate model robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that BGAN augmentation improves TabTransformer's Macro-F1 score from 82.96% to 86.50%, with the largest class-wise improvement observed for Web_Attack (F1 score: 0.29 to 0.61). Robustness evaluation shows that all non-augmented models experienced a 100% Performance Drop Rate (PDR) under adversarial testing, whereas all BGAN-augmented models achieved negative PDR values, indicating improved resilience. Furthermore, the augmented TabTransformer maintained stable and low False Triggered Rate (FTR) values (1.51%-2.92%) across all noise levels, compared with the BGAN-augmented Decision Tree, which reached 49.09% under benign perturbations. These findings demonstrate that BGAN consistently enhances both class balance and adversarial robustness, while the proposed BGAN-TabTransformer framework provides an effective and adaptive intrusion detection solution for adversarial network environments.
tldr: This paper applies a GAN-augmented TabTransformer for intrusion detection, focusing on class imbalance and adversarial robustness.
motivation: Machine learning-based IDS suffer from class imbalance and adversarial attacks, degrading performance.
method: The authors augment TabTransformer with Boundary-Seeking GAN to generate synthetic minority samples and adversarial samples, evaluated on CICIDS2017 dataset.
result: BGAN augmentation improves Macro-F1 from 82.96% to 86.50% and yields negative PDR under adversarial testing, indicating improved robustness.
conclusion: The BGAN-TabTransformer framework effectively enhances both class balance and adversarial robustness for intrusion detection.

title: Identity-Bound Academic Credentials On Blockchain: On-Chain Issuer Accreditation With Erc-3643 And OnchainID
authors: Gon\c{c}alo Frutuoso, Diogo Rodrigues, Alexandre P. Francisco, C\'atia Vaz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Verifying academic credentials remains difficult: records are held by individual institutions in proprietary systems, verification is slow and manual, and counterfeit qualifications are widespread. Blockchain-based registries have been proposed as a remedy, but existing systems tend to anchor certificate hashes without binding them to a verifiable identity, without an explicit mechanism to accredit issuing institutions, and without support for correcting or revoking credentials once issued. This paper investigates whether an infrastructure designed for regulated financial instruments can be repurposed to close these gaps. We present the design of a registry for identity-bound academic credentials that composes OnchainID self-sovereign identities (ERC-734/ERC-735) with the T-REX suite (ERC-3643): its trusted-issuer registry becomes an on-chain issuer-accreditation whitelist, and each certificate is represented as a signed, updatable claim bound to a student's identity and verifiable by any third party without a wallet, while sensitive fields are kept off-chain. We make explicit the tension between a transferable-security-token standard and non-transferable credentials, clarifying which of its guarantees carry over. We validate the design with a reference implementation covering the full certificate life cycle and evaluate it in terms of gas cost, scalability, latency, and security, quantifying the overhead relative to a hash-anchoring baseline.
tldr: This paper proposes a blockchain-based system for identity-bound academic credentials using ERC-3643 and OnchainID, focusing on issuer accreditation and credential lifecycle management.
motivation: Current academic credential verification is slow, manual, and prone to fraud; existing blockchain solutions lack binding to verifiable identities and issuer accreditation mechanisms.
method: The design composes OnchainID self-sovereign identities (ERC-734/ERC-735) with the T-REX suite (ERC-3643) to create an on-chain issuer accreditation whitelist and represent certificates as signed, updatable claims bound to student identities.
result: A reference implementation covering the full certificate lifecycle is presented, with evaluation of gas cost, scalability, latency, and security compared to a hash-anchoring baseline.
conclusion: The system addresses gaps in existing blockchain credential registries but is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Control-Driven Framework For Secure SaaS Onboarding In Regulated Enterprises
authors: Rithika Dulam Naga Sundeep Krishna Thota
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As enterprises increasingly adopt Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platforms for mission-critical functions, onboarding these services has emerged as a complex challenge extending well beyond procurement and basic security review. In regulated environments, SaaS onboarding must address multiple interdependent control domains, including Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM), cybersecurity assessment, Identity and Access Management (IAM), and disaster recovery (DR), which are often executed in isolation, resulting in delayed go-lives, duplicated assessments, unclear ownership, and residual operational risk. This paper proposes a control-driven, end-to-end SaaS onboarding framework that integrates TPRM, cybersecurity, IAM, and DR into a unified lifecycle model. The framework introduces a stage-based approach spanning intake and risk scoping, architecture validation, identity design, resilience assessment, and post-production governance. Key contributions include: (1) a structured SaaS onboarding lifecycle emphasizing sequencing and dependency management across control domains; (2) a cross-domain control mapping highlighting failure modes caused by siloed reviews; and (3) practical design patterns for secure connectivity, federated identity, least-privilege access, and shared-responsibility disaster recovery. Supported by operational lessons from enterprise-scale implementations and a reference governance checklist, the framework helps organizations reduce onboarding friction, improve auditability, and strengthen the security and resilience posture of SaaS-enabled platforms.
tldr: This paper proposes a control-driven framework for secure SaaS onboarding in regulated enterprises, focusing on integrating TPRM, cybersecurity, IAM, and DR into a unified lifecycle.
motivation: SaaS onboarding in regulated environments is complex and often siloed, leading to delays and residual risk.
method: The framework introduces a stage-based approach with cross-domain control mapping and practical design patterns.
result: Key contributions include a structured onboarding lifecycle, cross-domain control mapping, and design patterns for secure connectivity and identity management.
conclusion: The framework helps reduce onboarding friction, improve auditability, and strengthen security and resilience posture.

title: Towards Secure And Trustworthy DAOs For Cross-Chain Governance
authors: Faisal Haque Bappy, Tahrim Hossain, Tarannum Shaila Zaman, Tariqul Islam
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-chain DAOs face unique security challenges that go beyond traditional single-chain vulnerabilities. This paper identifies and categorizes four critical attack vectors in cross-chain DAO governance: bribery attacks, token control exploits, human-computer interaction deceptions, and protocol vulnerabilities. We propose a comprehensive security framework with a multi-layered architecture that integrates cryptographic trust anchors, fraud-resistant consensus mechanisms, and decentralized validation techniques to address these threats. Our framework introduces novel components, including a Governance Kernel with on-chain rule verification, a Cross-Chain Trust Layer using threshold cryptography, and a Resilience Layer offering time-locked decision reversals and progressive dispute resolution. By establishing a structured set of countermeasures, this work lays the foundation for secure, transparent, and attack-resistant governance across diverse blockchain environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a security framework for cross-chain DAOs, addressing attack vectors like bribery and token control exploits.
motivation: Cross-chain DAOs face unique security challenges beyond traditional single-chain vulnerabilities, requiring a comprehensive security framework.
method: The authors identify four critical attack vectors and propose a multi-layered architecture including a Governance Kernel, Cross-Chain Trust Layer using threshold cryptography, and a Resilience Layer with time-locked decision reversals.
result: The framework introduces novel components for on-chain rule verification, fraud-resistant consensus, and decentralized validation.
conclusion: This work lays a foundation for secure, transparent, and attack-resistant governance across diverse blockchain environments.

title: Transmit Coefficients And Receive Combining Vector Design For Ota-fl With Imperfect Csi
authors: Xiaoyan Ma, Shahryar Zehtabi, Yinan Zou, Taejoon Kim, Christopher G. Brinton
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) computation has recently gained significant attentions as an effective approach to enhance the communication efficiency of wireless federated learning (FL). By enabling simultaneous transmission and aggregation of local model updates, OTA-FL can substantially reduce both latency and bandwidth consumption. However, a key challenge lies in the imperfect aggregation of global models caused by channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, which introduces distortion to the final learning performance. To address this issue, we study the long-term mean squared error (MSE) minimization problem for OTA-FL under imperfect CSI conditions. Through convergence analysis, we establish an upper bound for the time-averaged MSE, thereby revealing the effect of aggregation errors accumulated throughout multiple communication rounds on the overall training performances. Based on this analysis, an optimization framework is developed to minimize the long-term MSE via the joint design of (i) transmit coefficients at the local devices and (ii) receive combining vectors at the parameter server (PS). Since this alternating optimization approach requires non-causal CSI, a Lyapunov-based optimization method is further introduced to handle causal CSI scenarios. By incorporating virtual queues to characterize long-term energy consumption, the proposed method effectively decouples temporal dependencies and allows transmit coefficients to be optimized based on the causal CSI of each aggregation round. Comprehensive evaluations on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets have demonstrated that the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the degradation of test accuracy caused by imperfect CSI. Comparisons with other benchmark schemes further verify the superiority of our proposed algorithms.
tldr: This paper addresses transmit coefficient and receive combining vector design for over-the-air federated learning under imperfect CSI, focusing on communication efficiency and MSE minimization.
motivation: Imperfect CSI in OTA-FL causes aggregation errors that degrade learning performance; existing methods assume perfect CSI or ignore long-term effects.
method: The authors derive an upper bound on time-averaged MSE via convergence analysis, then propose an alternating optimization framework for joint design of transmit coefficients and receive combining vectors, extended to causal CSI via Lyapunov optimization.
result: Proposed algorithms significantly reduce test accuracy degradation on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 compared to benchmarks.
conclusion: Joint optimization of transmit and receive parameters under imperfect CSI improves OTA-FL performance, with Lyapunov-based method enabling causal implementation.

title: A Multi-Model Hybrid Defense Approach Against White-box Adversarial Attacks In Computer Network Traffic
authors: Khushnaseeb Roshan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.17105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is crucial to safeguard computer networks from evolving network security threats and unknown cyberattacks. An essential tool for protecting computer networks against unknown cyber threats is Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS). However, NIDS faces a major security concern due to its susceptibility to adversarial attacks. Adversarial attacks aim to deceive NIDS by crafting and injecting adversarial examples into the system. These adversarial inputs can deceive the NIDS into misclassifying benign network traffic as malicious. We developed a resilient hybrid defense mechanism aimed to mitigate the impact of two potent adversarial attacks: Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and Carlini & Wagner (C&W) attack. Our hybrid defense approach leverages the combined strength of two heuristic defense methods: Adversarial Training (AT) and Gaussian Data Augmentation (GDA). GDA provides multi-directional defense, while AT enhances NIDS robustness against specific adversarial vectors. Under pre-attack scenarios, NIDS demonstrated good accuracy and f1-score. However, in the post-attack scenario, its accuracy significantly dropped under FGSM and C&W attacks (0.2649 and 0.4961, respectively). Our proposed hybrid defense method effectively mitigated these adversarial threats, with post-defense accuracy of 96.57% and 89.20% for FGSM and C&W attacks. We evaluated the defense strategy across a range of epsilon and confidence noise factor values (ranging from 0.0001 to 0.0009). This research provides a good direction for future researchers in the emerging area of adversarial machine learning from a security perspective.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid defense combining adversarial training and Gaussian data augmentation to protect network intrusion detection systems against white-box adversarial attacks.
motivation: Network intrusion detection systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that can cause misclassification of benign traffic as malicious, posing a security threat.
method: The hybrid defense combines Adversarial Training (AT) and Gaussian Data Augmentation (GDA) to mitigate FGSM and C&W attacks on a NIDS model.
result: Post-defense accuracy improved to 96.57% for FGSM and 89.20% for C&W attacks, compared to pre-defense drops to 0.2649 and 0.4961 respectively.
conclusion: The hybrid defense effectively mitigates adversarial threats in network traffic classification, providing a direction for future research in adversarial machine learning for security.

title: Dsa Nonce Vulnerabilities: An Interactive Analysis
authors: Rundong Wei, Xiaomei Tian, Xiaoqi Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.17107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital signatures are fundamental to identity authentication and data integrity in cybersecurity, and the NIST-standardized Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) frequently appears in the cryptography track of CTF competitions. However, DSA relies on number theory, modular arithmetic, and large-integer computation, making both the algorithm and its associated attacks difficult for beginners to follow. Conventional tools often expose only inputs and outputs, leaving the intermediate computations of signing, verification, and key-recovery attacks opaque. This paper presents a DSA signature analysis and visualisation platform tailored to CTF competitions. The platform provides three main capabilities: basic signature generation and verification, reproduction of common CTF attack methods, and dynamic visualisation of attack workflows. It covers three representative nonce vulnerabilities: nonce reuse, linear nonce leakage, and HNP-based lattice attacks. Stepwise displays and highlighted intermediate values make the underlying computations directly inspectable. Experiments show that the platform correctly reproduces the standard DSA workflow and all three attack scenarios.
tldr: A platform for visualizing DSA signature generation and attacks on nonce vulnerabilities, tailored for CTF competitions.
motivation: DSA and its attacks are hard for beginners to follow; existing tools lack intermediate computation visibility.
method: Developed an interactive platform that performs DSA signing, verification, and three nonce-based attacks (nonce reuse, linear leakage, HNP lattice) with stepwise visualization.
result: The platform correctly reproduces standard DSA workflow and all three attack scenarios.
conclusion: The platform aids CTF participants in understanding DSA vulnerabilities through dynamic visualization.

title: SpexPay: A Privacy-Preserving Pay-As-You-Go System For Dynamic Spectrum Sharing
authors: Mohaimin Al Barat, Hexuan Yu, Shaoyu Li, Yang Xiao, Yi Shi, Eric W. Burger, Y. Thomas Hou, Wenjing Lou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.17218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS) is a cornerstone of next-generation wireless systems, yet existing solutions such as Spectrum Access Systems (SAS) rely on centralized administrators that expose sensitive operational metadata and lack cryptographic transaction accountability. Though SAS administrators, such as Google, have introduced pay-as-you-go pricing models, these approaches still face significant privacy and accountability challenges as DSS evolves toward a more open and large-scale spectrum marketplace. We present SpexPay, a privacy-preserving and auditable pay-as-you-go spectrum usage framework that enforces fine-grained, usage-linked payments without revealing user identities. Spexpay integrates BBS+ verifiable credentials, unlinkable session pseudonyms, and selective-disclosure proofs to enforce privacy-preserving access authorization, while leveraging Solidity-based smart contracts to realize automated and non-repudiable escrow settlement. By recording only pseudonymous usage evidence and hash-chained metering data on-chain, the system achieves strong unlinkability while preserving verifiable accountability and auditability. A full prototype demonstrates low end-to-end latency ([MATH]150 ms) and modest on-chain cost ([MATH]603K gas or [MATH]\$0.9), showing that SpexPay is practical for real-world DSS deployments. We also evaluated the user-side cryptographic operations on a Raspberry Pi 5 to assess scalability and suitability for edge-class hardware. Our code and artifacts are publicly available at [URL].
tldr: SpexPay is a privacy-preserving pay-as-you-go system for dynamic spectrum sharing using blockchain and verifiable credentials.
motivation: Existing dynamic spectrum sharing solutions like SAS lack privacy and accountability; SpexPay aims to provide fine-grained usage payments without revealing user identities.
method: The system integrates BBS+ verifiable credentials, unlinkable session pseudonyms, selective-disclosure proofs, and Solidity smart contracts for automated escrow settlement.
result: A prototype demonstrates low end-to-end latency (<150 ms) and modest on-chain cost (~$0.9), with cryptographic operations feasible on Raspberry Pi 5.
conclusion: SpexPay is practical for real-world DSS deployments, offering strong privacy and accountability.

title: Measuring And Evaluating The Performance Of Generative Ai Models For Scam Detection
authors: Cem Topcuoglu, Seyed Ali Akhavani, Harel Berger, Sadia Afroz, Michalis Pachilakis, Vibhor Sehgal, Leyla Bilge, Engin Kirda
abstract: ArXiv:2607.17353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online scams continue to cause substantial financial and personal harm. As a result, detection systems based on Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated into security products ranging from email gateways and browser extensions to fraud-monitoring dashboards. As this adoption accelerates, a common belief has taken hold: that these models are broadly suitable for scam detection. In this work, we investigate whether LLMs, with their strong capabilities in understanding intent, context, and reasoning, can effectively detect scams across diverse scenarios without task-specific fine-tuning. We curate and release a unique benchmark dataset of real-world scams spanning multiple formats and topics. We evaluate nine LLMs of varying sizes and architectures, examining their performance under different prompting strategies and comparing them to a fine-tuned BERT-based classifier. Our results show that while larger LLMs generally outperform smaller ones, effective prompting substantially boosts the performance of smaller models. Moreover, LLMs are better at generalizing to unseen scams compared to fine-tuned models, suggesting that pre-trained knowledge contributes meaningfully to scam detection. We release our dataset and evaluation framework to facilitate future research in robust scam detection using language models.
tldr: This paper evaluates the performance of generative AI models for detecting online scams across diverse scenarios without task-specific fine-tuning.
motivation: Online scams cause substantial harm, and LLMs are increasingly used in security products, but their general suitability for scam detection without fine-tuning is not well understood.
method: The authors curate a benchmark dataset of real-world scams and evaluate nine LLMs of varying sizes under different prompting strategies, comparing them to a fine-tuned BERT-based classifier.
result: Larger LLMs generally outperform smaller ones, but effective prompting substantially boosts smaller models; LLMs generalize better to unseen scams than fine-tuned models.
conclusion: Pre-trained knowledge in LLMs contributes meaningfully to scam detection, and the released dataset and framework can facilitate future research.

title: Optical Shaping Of Nanoplasma Shockwaves
authors: Jacopo Fregoni

tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for scalar transport in fluid dynamics, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve stability and accuracy of lattice Boltzmann simulations for high-Péclet number scalar transport.
method: Combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with nonorthogonality correction and a realizability limiter.
result: The method achieves stable and accurate simulations at high Péclet numbers.
conclusion: The proposed RELBM is effective for high-Péclet scalar transport problems.

result: Obtains explicit analytical solutions for ring solitons and lump waves, demonstrating their propagation and interaction properties.

Using neutron inelastic scattering, the authors investigate the dynamics of liquid hydrogen sulfide, which is similar to water but lacks the hydrogen-bond network. While fast sound is preserved, the secondary weakly dispersive mode typical of hydrogen-bonded liquids is not detected.

motivation: To understand the role of hydrogen bonding in the dynamics of liquids by comparing water with its non-hydrogen-bonded analog, hydrogen sulfide.
method: Neutron inelastic scattering experiments on liquid hydrogen sulfide to measure its dynamic structure factor and identify collective modes.
result: Fast sound is preserved in hydrogen sulfide, but the secondary weakly dispersive mode characteristic of hydrogen-bonded liquids is absent.
conclusion: The absence of the secondary mode confirms its association with hydrogen-bond networks, highlighting the unique dynamics of hydrogen-bonded liquids.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition and scope of active matter as a subset of nonequilibrium systems, including recent developments like nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its meaning and provide a precise definition.
method: The authors review the history and current usage of the term, propose a definition, and survey recent developments in the field.
result: They offer a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems and highlight emerging topics such as quantum active matter.
conclusion: A clear definition helps unify the field and guide future research, but the paper is a review without novel technical contributions to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using a scanning probe as an optical antenna.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with optical fluorescence, using the tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides new insights into molecular identification and reactions at the atomic scale.
